Real Betis will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume domestic affairs at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday afternoon.

The Seville outfit lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 21 victories to Rayo's 13, while 16 of their 50 previous matches have finished all square.

Real Betis will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-0 win over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, with the result leaving them sixth in the overall table, claiming 12 points from their five games in the league stage of the tournament.

Manuel Pellegrini's side boast a record of eight wins, three draws and two defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 27 points leaving them in fourth spot in the La Liga table, five points ahead of fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

Real Betis are only four points behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, but they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sevilla in the Seville derby last weekend.

El Glorioso were last victorious in the league on November 8, beating Elche 2-0, while their last defeat at this level was a 5-2 home reverse to Barcelona on October 17.

Real Betis will be in Copa del Rey action against CD Extremadura on December 1 before facing Atletico Madrid in La Liga ahead of their next Champions League fixture with Como.

Rayo, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of successive defeats to Real Sociedad and Valencia in Spain's top flight, and it has been a tough season to date for the capital outfit.

Benat San Jose's side have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches to sit in 16th spot in the division on 12 points, level on points with 18th-placed Getafe.

Rayo have the third-worst away record in Spain's top flight this season, picking up just two points from six matches, which is a concern ahead of this game.

Los Franjirrojos have actually drawn their last four matches against Real Betis, while they have not been beaten by the Seville outfit since September 2023.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw in the corresponding game during the 2025-26 campaign, and it was also 1-1 when they locked horns in the same stadium in December 2024.

Antony and Isco are both set to retain their spots in the final third of the field, while Pablo Fornals is likely to be joined by Marc Roca in the middle of the midfield.

As for Rayo, Augusto Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin are out through injury, but the capital outfit have no fresh fitness concerns.

Sergio Camello has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 13 appearances, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be another spot at centre-forward for Randy Nteka despite the fact that the 28-year-old is still waiting for his first goal of the campaign.

Breaking: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

In a recent development, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the newly introduced exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, claims exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

According to recent reports, alongside Picasso, a surprising number of important artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Recent findings suggest that bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

Two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

However, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

According to recent reports, the dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked big and dangerous.".

Industry observers note that the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian claims. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a upcoming image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

It has been revealed that the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

Still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

In a recent development, but altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

Industry observers note that the feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

In a recent development, "It's really crazy," she says, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

The Blues head to the City Ground on Friday night looking to get back to winning ways after successive Premier League losses, with a 4-1 home thrashing by their old rivals following a 1-0 defeat at struggling Sunderland prior to the international break.

Xabi Alonso’s side have been criticised for their poor defending and a perceived lack of intensity in recent performances, and summer signing Chavarria is keen for them to put that right against a Forest team that right now sit nine places below them in the table.

“We have to give a lot more because, in the end, we’re at a club where the demands are at a different level,” he told Chelsea’s official media channels.

“We know the responsibility we have and I think we’ve realised that we can’t repeat a match like that [the Leeds game] again.

“Obviously, on any given day we can win, we can lose, or we can draw, but the attitude we had, I think, wasn’t right, and we players know that it was our fault. So we’re already mentally focused on going all out with the bit between our teeth.

“We’re going to treat Nottingham Forest like it’s the last game we play, and we truly believe it, we take it seriously. That’s the only way, because football now is so competitive that any team can beat you.

“We are clear that we want to work and we want to be a competitive team, so the only way forward is to stay united and work even harder.”.

Chavarria, who joined Chelsea for £16.3million from Rayo Vallecano in August, continued: “I think it will be like these last two games we had against Sunderland and Leeds – very physical teams playing with a back five, playing very directly, with very powerful and quality players up front.

In a recent development, “Ultimately, it will be a hard-fought match with a lot of individual duels, decided by small details, like most games are. We have to stay extremely focused so that we land the first blow.”.

Industry observers note that discussing his own performances, the 28-year-old added: “I’m trying to give my absolute best. I know I can give a lot more. I think in these matches that progression is going to show.”.

Arsenal versus Manchester City has emerged as the standout Premier League fixture in recent years.

And even before the end of November, Sunday's showdown at the Emirates Stadium could have huge ramifications for the rest of the season.

After City started their first campaign under Enzo Maresca with seven straight victories, a four-game winless run has allowed Arsenal to pull six points clear at the summit.

Will they put further distance between themselves and last season's runners-up on Sunday, or will City turn things around?

Here, we delve into the best Opta insights to provide a data-powered preview of this weekend's standout fixture.

Next up: Arsenal   #AsahiSuperDry https://t.co/QKUTHnEP2v.

An Arsenal victory would give them a huge advantage even at this very early stage in the title race, and the supercomputer fancies them to get the job done.

Across 10,000 data-led simulations conducted by the model, Arsenal were victorious in 54.4% of scenarios.

City, meanwhile, are assigned a 22.2% chance of taking all three points and a 23.4% probability of leaving north London with a draw.

City traditionally dominated this fixture, but Mikel Arteta has managed to tip the scales in Arsenal's favour in recent years.

Having lost six consecutive home league games against City between 2018 and 2023, Arsenal are now unbeaten in their last three against them at Emirates Stadium (W2 D1).

Overall, City have only won one of the last six Premier League games between the sides (D3 L2), though that victory did come when they last met in the competition this April (2-1 at Etihad Stadium).

A better omen for City is the fact they have won 12 of their last 14 top-flight games against the reigning champions (D1 L1), completing the double over Liverpool last season.

They have lost three of their four games when facing Arsenal as champions in the competition, though, drawing the other 1-1 in January 2005.

Things to work on for Arsenal after drab draws.

Arsenal's lead over City in the table could have been even more commanding, if not for a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James' Park last weekend.

Arteta's side have been tremendous on their own turf this season, though – they are the only Premier League side yet to drop a single point at home in 2026-27.

The Gunners are on an eight-match winning run in home Premier League games, their longest since a 10-match streak between April and December in 2022, though they were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Champions League nights   Shot by Josh Upton https://t.co/FaaF2uuoJA.

Arsenal have, of course, already beaten City once this season, running out convincing 3-0 victors in the Community Shield in August.

But the Gunners have not beaten City twice in the same campaign since 2014-15 – with one of those wins coming by a 3-0 scoreline in the Community Shield – and aspects of last week's performance on Tyneside will certainly have displeased Arteta.

In the first half of that game, Arsenal only gave up three shots, none of which were on target, but in the second period, Newcastle had nine attempts and hit the target with three of them.

Though Noni Madueke's goal salvaged a point for the champions after Newcastle fought back to go 2-1 up, that was Arsenal's only shot on target after half-time, from two total attempts.

Arsenal's problem against Dortmund was not chance creation, though; it was their finishing, having put up 30 shots and 2.8 expected goals to BVB's 13 and 1.12 xG.

Captain Martin Odegaard has been one of the league's best playmakers this season, and he is now just two assists away from tying Morten Gamst Pedersen's record for the most by a Norwegian player in the Premier League (38; Pedersen managed 40).

Since the start of 2023-24, only Bruno Fernandes (41) and Mohamed Salah (35) have bettered Odegaard's 25 Premier League assists.

Pressure on for Haaland and City.

Odegaard will, of course, be going up against his Norway team-mate Erling Haaland, who has been a constant thorn in Arsenal's side ever since he arrived in the Premier League.

Haaland has scored in each of his last four Premier League games against Arsenal and could now become just the fourth player to net in five straight matches against them in the competition, after Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink in September 2000, Harry Kane in April 2017 and Charlie Austin in December 2018.

The goals have dried up for Haaland lately, however, after he found the net nine times in his first eight Premier League outings of 2026-27.

He has since failed to score in his last three Premier League games, despite totalling 25 touches in the opposing area, 12 shots and exactly 2.0 xG versus Brighton, Nottingham Forest and Fulham.

He could now equal his worst-ever goal drought in the English top flight, having previously failed to score in four consecutive games between February and April this year, against Newcastle, Forest, West Ham and Chelsea.

But Haaland is certainly not the only City player whose performances have dipped lately, and a 2-2 Champions League draw with Napoli in midweek will have done little to lift their spirits.

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 24, 2026.

Since the start of matchday eight, bottom side Crystal Palace (0) are the only team to pick up fewer points than City (one).

They are just the second side in English Football League history to win their first seven games of a season before going winless in their next four, along with Sheffield Wednesday in the 1904-05 top flight.

According to recent reports, and their defensive record of late has also proved a real worry. City have conceded the first goal in each of their last four Premier League games.

They last had a longer run in March/April 2012 (five), the fifth game of which was a 1-0 loss at Arsenal with current Gunners boss Arteta netting the winner.

City's terrible run has seen their title chances – in the eyes of the Opta supercomputer, at least – dip to just 9.1%, compared to Arsenal's 76.7%. If they are beaten this weekend, a recovery may already be beyond them.

Havertz scored Arsenal's second goal when they thrashed City in the Community Shield three months ago, maintaining his strong record against the Citizens.

The German has been involved in four goals in his last four games against City in all competitions (three goals, one assist).

Viktor Gyokeres started up front against Dortmund, but given how much Arteta trusts Havertz out of possession, he should return following his midweek rest.

  • Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.
  • The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33.

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are at the moment some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary concerns against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose matter.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

Moreirense possible starting lineup:.

A Ferreira; Pinto, Kevyn Monteiro, Batista, A Martinez; N John, Liberato; Andrade, Mendonca, Landerson; Vonic.

Santa Clara possible starting lineup:.

Franca; Lucas Soares, Ythallo, H Silva, Fofana; Tavares, Borges, Vasconcelos; V Lopes, Paciencia, B Lucas.

Santa Clara have been considerably stronger away from home this season, but their defensive absences could prove costly against a Moreirense side that have won three of the last four meetings between the clubs.

Furthermore, the hosts have an opportunity to exploit an inexperienced centre-back pairing, although their own scoring problems and the visitors' impressive away record suggest neither side will have enough to claim all three points.

In a recent development, manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It has been revealed that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

In a recent development, “It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously noted of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Chelsea are facing a potential problem surrounding Alejandro Garnacho.

The Argentine, firmly out of favour at Stamford Bridge, joined Aston Villa in the summer on a loan deal which included a conditional obligation to make the move permanent for £42.5million at the end of the season.

Industry observers note that while the conditions that would trigger Garnacho’s permanent exit remain undisclosed, they are believed to involve the player making a certain number of appearances which Chelsea sources described at the time as easily achievable. Villa are also paying a loan fee.

However, with Garnacho being left out of four of Villa’s last five matchday squads, there is now growing doubt over whether the 22-year-old’s Chelsea exit will become permanent.

Chelsea placed a public valuation of £43m on Garnacho in July once the club’s hierarchy decided they wanted to sell him.

Garnacho’s initial preference had been to move overseas, and there was interest from Saudi Arabia, Serie A and elsewhere in Europe, until Villa made their interest known, shortly after selling their best player, Morgan Rogers, to Chelsea for £117m.

Garnacho has featured in just seven of Villa’s 19 games across all competitions so far this season, and is yet to start for Unai Emery’s side.

Garnacho’s exile continued this week in the Champions League clash at Galatasaray, where Emery decided to name just 11 out of a possible 12 substitutes - two of which were goalkeepers.

When asked about Garnacho’s latest absence, Emery noted: “The players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.”.

The Athletic have since reported that Villa are exploring their options to get rid of the player in January, though it remains to be seen if Chelsea would welcome such talks.

Chelsea and Villa could jointly agree to terminate the loan agreement, which would allow Garnacho to explore options elsewhere. But that would require both clubs agreeing to do so, and the chances of Chelsea getting a fee similar to the £42.5m Villa had committed to again appear slim.

The situation is threatening to become a headache which Chelsea believed they had remedied.

Chelsea may instead point to the chance that Garnacho’s minutes improve in the second half of the campaign as reason to keep the Argentine in situ.

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:49.

Coming off a three-week break from competitive action, Academico de Viseu and Alverca meet at Estadio do Fontelo on Saturday evening in what will be their first-ever encounter in Portugal's top flight.

The hosts occupy sixth place in the Primeira Liga table, eight points and five positions ahead of their visitors, who are four points above the relegation play-off spot.

Academico de Viseu have made an encouraging return to the top flight after a 37-year absence, having collected six wins from their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L3), scoring 15 times and conceding 13 at the other end.

Bruno Pinheiro's side, who failed to record a victory in any of their first four outings this term, enjoyed a particularly impressive spell between September 6 and November 1, winning six consecutive league matches, including a famous triumph away to Sporting Lisbon on October 25.

However, that winning run in the top flight came to an end last time out, when the Viseu club suffered a 1-0 defeat to Nacional in Funchal after conceding a late winner to Matchoi Djalo.

The result also means Academico have now alternated between defeats and victories across their last five matches in all competitions, including cup losses to lower-division Fatima in the Taca de Portugal and Primeira Liga champions Porto in the Taca da Liga.

Returning from a three-week hiatus, the Viseu club will be glad to be back at Fontelo, where they have won each of their last three matches, beating Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estoril Praia and Rio Ave by 2-1 scorelines after losing their opening two fixtures at the ground this term.

Like the hosts, Alverca also started the campaign slowly, failing to record a victory in any of their opening five fixtures, but enjoyed a three-match winning run between September 12 and October 12, beating Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao.

However, the Ribatejo club have slipped back into familiar struggles, having since gone winless in four matches across all competitions, starting with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of second-tier Tondela before suffering narrow league defeats against Arouca and Benfica.

Sergio Ferreira's team then drew 1-1 with Casa Pia in their most recent outing, with Ian Luccas finding the net in the 66th minute to rescue a point, while the goal ended a three-match run without scoring.

Two wins from their last three league games on the road suggest Alverca have also held their own away from home, although they have been vulnerable when not at their best, losing three of their five away league outings this season.

There is also little to draw from history, given the Ribatejo club are without a victory in their previous three meetings with Academico, losing twice in that spell, although their most recent visit to Viseu ended in a 2-2 draw in February 2025 in Liga 2.

With no reported injury or suspension concerns, Academico head coach Pinheiro could retain a similar lineup to the one that featured against Nacional, with goalkeeper Ewerton shielded by the defensive quartet of Anthony Correia, Nikolaos Michelis, Robinho and Miguel Angel Brau.

Andre Clovis has scored five of the Viseu club's 15 league goals this season and also provided an assist, with the Brazilian expected to lead the line here.

Alverca could be without Rayan Lucas, who remains a doubt after suffering another setback with his left knee, although the midfielder has returned to integrated training.

Nabil Touaizi is also expected to miss out after suffering a relapse of a right-calf injury, while Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai remain sidelined following knee surgery.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Noah Raveyre is another absentee, with his return expected in early December.

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:.

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Guilherme, Kahraman, Mortimer; Clovis.

Alverca possible starting lineup:.

Mendes; Boyan, Gomez, James; Spencer, I Luccas, Gui, Chissumba; Chiquinho, Camara, Figueiredo.

Academico have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, but their overall league form and stronger position in the table make them worthy favourites against an Alverca side that have scored just once in their last four matches, so a home victory looks plausible.

Latest Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has called on Yeremy Pino to improve his disciplinary record.

The Spanish attacker has been one of Palace’s better players in a difficult season, but is suspended for Sunday’s clash with Hull after picking up his fifth yellow card of the Premier League season in last weekend’s 3-2 defeat at Coventry.

Pino was also booked in Thursday’s 2-1 Europa League win over 10-man Real Sociedad, and Frank admitted discipline was something the 24-year-old would have to work on.

“Yes, I think it’s fair to say,” Frank said. “I think he’s a very good player — very vital for us and has gone up a level this season — so of course it is disappointing.

According to recent reports, “It is something he needs to work on. That is too many yellow cards. Of course, we would have loved to play with Yeremy and [Ismaila] Sarr and JP [Jean-Philippe Mateta] in an crucial match — three of our best offensive players — but others will need to step up and show what they can do.”.

Asked whether Palace had picked up any new knocks against Sociedad, Frank replied: “Not that I am aware of, so hopefully not.”.

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table and have half the tally of 14 points 11th-place Hull have taken from their first 11 games.

“It will be difficult against a Hull team that is fighting with every inch of their bodies from all players on the pitch,” Frank mentioned.

Real Madrid's £68m Nico Paz transfer strategy faces fresh uncertainty as Jose Mourinho responds

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55.
  • Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.
  • The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.

The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.

Sources indicate that madrid retained the option to bring Paz back in the summer of 2027 when an agreement was reached with Como in June to allow the 22-year-old to continue his development in Serie A. However, despite recent suggestions that the Spanish giants have already decided to exercise that option, uncertainty remains over their aims.

Asked about Paz during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, Mourinho offered a typically brief response: "He's not my player.".

The Portuguese manager's reluctance to discuss a player contracted to another club should not be interpreted as opposition to the transfer, although his response offered little clarification following contrasting reports in the Spanish media.

Cadena COPE reported last week that Real Madrid intended to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option next summer, with Como having reportedly been informed of the decision.

However, according to Jose Felix Diaz of AS, Madrid have yet to reach a definitive conclusion and could wait until the spring before deciding whether to bring their former academy prospect back.

In a recent development, the club's official statement in June confirmed the existence of a unilateral buy-back option for the 2027-28 season. Crucially, the agreement allowing Paz to remain in Italy for another year was reached at the player's own request, underlining the importance he attaches to regular first-team football at this stage of his career.

The biggest sporting consideration for Madrid remains the presence of Jude Bellingham, whose performances under Mourinho have strengthened his position as the team's principal attacking midfielder.

Sources indicate that the England international has scored seven goals and provided five assists in 18 appearances this season, including a goal and an assist in Tuesday's 5-1 victory over PSV. Madrid are also reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new contract for Bellingham, whose existing agreement runs until 2029.

Paz's versatility would give Mourinho some scope to accommodate both players. The Argentine is capable of operating from the right or in a slightly deeper midfield position, although those roles would bring him into direct competition with Arda Guler, Brahim Diaz and Bernardo Silva.

According to recent reports, madrid must also consider how the squad will look next season, with Rodrygo expected to return from injury and Franco Mastantuono due back from his loan spell. Summer signing Yan Diomande represents another significant investment in the attacking department.

Spending £68m on Paz could still make considerable financial sense given his age, development and potential resale value. However, the circumstances that prompted him to remain at Como last summer have hardly changed, particularly with Bellingham enjoying such an influential role under Mourinho.

Waiting until the spring would allow Madrid to assess both Paz's progress and the needs of their own squad before committing to a substantial expenditure. With their final buy-back opportunity approaching, the Spanish giants must determine whether they can offer the Argentine the regular football that has allowed him to flourish in Italy.

Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.
  • In a recent development, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW.
  • Recent findings suggest that the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a child growing up in Australia, Louise Pain hated her surname.

In a recent development, "People used to tease me; I was called things like 'Pain in the a*s,'" she told DW. "I remember actively hating my surname when I was a child and wanting to change it.".

Recent findings suggest that the jokes have followed her throughout her life, even after she moved to Germany. But one thing did eventually change: Pain's feelings about her own name.

Industry observers note that names are not only a fundamental part of how we identify ourselves — they can, beyond teasing, also influence how other people treat us. So, what happens if we dislike our own name, or if it is perceived negatively by those around us?

"A person's name is vital to their sense of identity," psychoanalyst Mikita Brottman told DW. "When someone has an embarrassing name, that embarrassment can be incorporated into their identity.".

Research on name bias has linked negatively perceived names with romantic rejection,as well as lower educational outcomes, lower self-esteem and more frequent smoking.

This suggests that names could influence our life trajectory, namely through self-esteem and opportunity.

But a person's relationship with their name is not necessarily fixed. Pain's lived experience, and that of another woman with the first name Tiny, demonstrates how people can find ways to reclaim, and even come to value, names that once triggered ridicule and rejection.

Names can act as "signals" when you first meet someone, personality psychologist Jochen Gebauer told DW. Those signals may lose importance as people get to know each other, but Gebauer stated their effects could also accumulate over a lifetime, potentially contributing to "real measurable advantages and disadvantages.".

Research led by sociologist Anthony Lee found that a name can evoke inaccurate assumptions about intelligence, competence, trustworthiness, sociability and attractiveness. For Pain, other people's reactions have extended beyond jokes. In high school, a teacher refused to believe that 'Pain' was her real surname and reprimanded her in front of the class.

Industry observers note that "Your name couldn't possibly be Pain. Write your real name!" she recalled the teacher saying.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In Lee's UK-based research, less familiar names tended to fall along a dimension partly characterized as "weirdness," which may help explain why difficult-to-pronounce or culturally unfamiliar names receive more negative evaluations.

Tiny, now 54, encountered the same questions about her unfamiliar name growing up in Greece.

Her parents had adapted "Tiny" to "Tinie" to make it sound more Greek, but people would repeatedly ask what her real or baptismal name was.

It has been revealed that even relatives have refused to accept it. Recently, two elderly aunts introduced her to someone as "Haritini," a conventional Greek name.

"I didn't even bother correcting them at this point," Tiny told DW.

Tiny's relationship with her name has also evolved.

"The jokes [from others] got repetitive and boring pretty fast, so at least I was left with the sense that I have something unique with my name going on.".

Industry observers note that pain, now 40, discovered how much cultural context could change the reaction to her surname when she began learning her father's native French as a teenager. In French, 'pain' means bread.

"People started calling me 'Bread! Louise Bread.'".

It has been revealed that later, after moving to Germany, the jokes became mostly bread-related rather than the more scathing ones she had experienced in Australia. "That helped me to feel better about my name," she said.

As they got older, both Pain and Tiny developed coping strategies to pre-empt people's reactions to their names.

Sources indicate that tiny sometimes introduces herself with: "Hi, I'm Tiny. It's my name and not a statement," or, "I'm Tiny. Not a difficult name to live up to.".

"This usually stops people from asking awkward questions.".

Pain also began to embrace the humor surrounding her name.

"I was convinced that I should become either a doctor or a dominatrix, or perhaps both, to become either 'Doctor Pain,' or 'Mistress Pain.'".

"Names can conjure that whole spectrum of shame and pride," psychoanalyst Melissa Daum told DW.

Pain now finds that people tend to see her surname as "funny and endearing… it's become something that is more of a funny talking point.".

But the childhood discomfort has not entirely disappeared. When Pain thinks about having children, her feelings about the name become more complicated.

"I don't really want to pass on my surname ... so there is a deeper wound there.".

But Pain also believes her father would be deeply hurt if future children had a different name. The surname she once hated connects her to him and to her French heritage.

"Something that once feels like an inconvenience or a source of self-consciousness can become a marker of distinctiveness, history, or belonging," Daum noted.

Tiny describes a similar ambivalence.

"My parents seemingly made an unfortunate choice, but by now I have embraced both the name and the sense of uniqueness that comes with it.".

Industry observers note that that does not mean she uses Tiny everywhere. She avoids it on dating apps because "Tiny might give off the wrong message," and does not use it in her email address when she wants to appear professional.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Pain, meanwhile, uses a Germanized version of the French word for bread as her social media surname.

Online, people have more control over what name they present to others. As Daum put it: "Choosing one's own name can feel like an act of mastery, even a refusal of that original passivity: I will decide what I am called and how I am encountered.".

But accepting a name does not necessarily mean embracing it in every situation.

Pain once wanted to change her surname. Tiny considered using her middle name in her thirties. Neither ultimately abandoned the names that had caused them difficulties.

For Tiny, at least, a name that once made her feel awkward has become something she can imagine carrying for the rest of her life.

"It might be cute to eventually be a granny called Tiny.".

  • Vitoria de Guimaraes will look to end a three-match winless run across all competitions when they welcome Estrela Amadora to Estadio D.
  • The hosts sit 14th in the Primeira Liga table with nine points from 11 matches, just one point and two places behind the visitors, whose early-season resilience has begun to fade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 21:01.

Vitoria de Guimaraes will look to end a three-match winless run across all competitions when they welcome Estrela Amadora to Estadio D. Afonso Henriques on Saturday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the Primeira Liga table with nine points from 11 matches, just one point and two places behind the visitors, whose early-season resilience has begun to fade.

Vitoria endured their lowest league finish in eight years last term, ending the campaign in ninth place, and their efforts to climb back towards the higher reaches of the table this season have so far proved difficult.

Closer to the relegation zone than the European places, Tiago Margarido's side sit just one point above the relegation playoff spot and 11 behind fifth-placed Arouca, having managed only two wins from their opening 11 league matches (D3, L6).

With victories proving hard to come by, Vitoria have won just one of their eight league games (D3, L4) since beating Nacional on matchday three, with their most recent triumph coming in a 5-0 thrashing of Maritimo on October 23.

Margarido's side have since played out a goalless draw with Gil Vicente before suffering a 2-1 defeat to leaders Porto in their latest top-flight outing, leaving the Guimaraes club with 11 goals scored and 12 conceded in the league this season.

Vitoria suffered another setback at the weekend, when they were eliminated from the Taca de Portugal following a 2-0 defeat to Braga, meaning they have now lost consecutive matches at D. Afonso Henriques for the first time since December 2025.

Meanwhile, the Conquerors have collected eight points from six league matches (W2, D2, L2) at the Minho ground this season and will be looking to improve that tally with a positive result on Saturday.

Estrela, on the other hand, have seen their solid start to the campaign under manager Pepa fade, having now lost each of their last five league matches following an unbeaten run across their opening six fixtures.

While defeats to Academico, Arouca and Casa Pia were disappointing, the Tricolores' two most recent losses have been particularly painful, as they conceded stoppage-time winners in a 2-1 defeat to Moreirense and a 3-2 setback against Benfica.

As a result, Estrela have conceded at least twice in nine of their 11 league matches this season and shipped a total of 22 goals in the Primeira Liga campaign, with only Rio Ave (24) allowing more, while the Amadora club have scored 17 at the other end.

However, there was some encouragement in their most recent outing, as the Tricolores defeated Portimonense 1-0 in the Taca de Portugal to secure a place in the last 16 and record their first clean sheet in 13 matches.

While Estrela will look to build on that cup success, they have a poor away record to contend with heading into the weekend, having managed just one league victory in 14 away games this year (D5, L8).

The visitors have also struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last six league encounters and losing five, including a 2-1 defeat at D. Afonso Henriques in February.

Vitoria will be without Toni Borevkovic, who is suspended after collecting his fifth yellow card against Porto, with Thiago Balieiro expected to be the leading candidate to replace him in central defence.

The hosts have also suffered a major setback at left-back, as Joao Mendes has been ruled out for the rest of the season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament injury to his right knee, while backup Francisco Dias is also unavailable with a right foot sprain.

As a result, Tomas Rodrigues has been called up from the B team to provide cover on the left, although Mohammed Kebdani could feature there, while goalkeeper Juan Castillo has returned to training after an ankle injury but Lucas Furtado is expected to retain his place between the sticks.

Estrela have no reported suspensions, while Jeremy Arevalo is a doubt with a back problem that has prevented him from featuring for the Tricolores since joining from Stuttgart in the summer.

Eddy Doue and Beni Souza have been left out of recent squads for disciplinary reasons and remain doubts for Saturday's trip to Guimaraes.

Leandro Antonetti ended a six-match league goal drought by scoring against Benfica and presently leads the team with five Primeira Liga goals this season, a tally he will be looking to add to this weekend.

Ian Stoica also scored his first goal in seven matches with the winner against Portimonense in the domestic cup and will be keen to find greater consistency in front of goal.

Vitoria de Guimaraes possible starting lineup:.

Furtado; Strata, Balieiro, Sidibe, Kebdani; Nogueira, Mukendi; G Silva, Samu, Camara; Jakupovic.

Estrela Amadora possible starting lineup:.

Linck; Scholze, Schappo, L Patrick, R Soares; Jansson, Serra; Marcus, Zvonarek, Stoica; Antonetti.

Neither side has been convincing in recent weeks, but Vitoria's stronger head-to-head record and home advantage could give them the edge against an Estrela team that have lost five consecutive league matches, making a home victory look feasible.

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

It has been revealed that noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC.

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

It has been revealed that “We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

According to recent reports, “I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”.

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

According to recent reports, declan Rice can't hit the target! ❌ https://t.co/kZv0k0MluO.

Yet Madueke provided the crucial contribution, driving a right-footed shot towards goal which took a heavy deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha to beat Matz Sels.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a major moment for the winger.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke stated. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”.

It has been revealed that forest’s problems at home are increasing and Oliver Glasner is now the club’s fifth manager in a year to experience such problems. His team have now gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters. They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Mark Flekken believes Bayer Leverkusen are "well on their way" in the Europa League after a 2-0 win over Dinamo Zagreb.

Malik Tillman opened the scoring just 10 minutes in before Jarell Quansah made sure of the result on the stroke of half-time.

It was Leverkusen's fourth win from five games in the Europa League, after they bounced back from a 1-0 loss to Marseille last time out in the competition.

The result moved them up to fourth in the table, leaving them three points behind pacesetters Bournemouth, boosting their chances of earning an automatic spot in the knockout stage.

However, it was not a vintage attacking performance from Leverkusen, who scored with both of their shots on target while only having nine attempts worth 1.3 expected goals (xG) overall.

And while Flekken was thrilled to get the victory, he noted how key it will be to put a bigger emphasis on attacking more in their next games.

"We did well in the first half; in the second, we were a bit weaker," he said.

"We'll certainly take one or two points away to analyse, but overall, it was a good match.

Recent findings suggest that "We're now well on our way with twelve points. But of course, the motto for the next match is: go on the attack!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Victor Munoz has avoided serious injury in a boost for Liverpool, who will likely remain without both Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch for Sunday’s Merseyside derby against Everton.

The Reds were handed a fresh fitness scare on Wednesday night as summer signing Munoz limped off shortly before half-time in their 3-0 away win over Club Brugge in the Champions League.

The Spanish winger was hurt after a strong challenge that came at the end of a brilliant run and received treatment on the pitch before going off and being replaced by Rio Ngumoha.

Any fears over a long-term lay-off have now been allayed, however, with Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola revealing that Munoz could return to training as soon as Saturday.

According to recent reports, “With Victor, I think the good news is that after assessing him, there is no disruption in the knee, everything is fine,” Iraola mentioned at his pre-Everton press conference on Friday. “But he has a big knock. It’s a big knock.

Sources indicate that “He hasn’t trained today but he wants to try tomorrow. We’ll see how the bruise is. But I cannot tell you right now.”.

Liverpool will definitely still be missing Gakpo against Everton, with the Netherlands forward set to sit out the third match in a row with a calf injury sustained on international duty.

“Cody definitely not [available against Everton],” Iraola remarked. “It’s a muscle injury so we have to wait a little bit until the process goes on and it heals.

“This kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last [Netherlands] game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline.

“But normally I don’t like to say timelines with injuries because every injury is different and some of them go quicker than others.

“It wasn’t a massive injury but there is something there and you have to give the time to heal.”.

Gakpo’s Dutch team-mate Gravenberch also seems unlikely to return for Liverpool against Everton as he continues to deal with heel pain, having not played at all for club or country since the Carabao Cup last-16 win over Chelsea a month ago.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s going to be difficult,” Iraola stated of the chances of the midfielder being available for Sunday’s short trip to the Hill Dickinson Stadium. “I cannot say no because these kinds of injuries are difficult.

“They don’t look like a major thing but you have the pain, it doesn’t go. Sometimes it’s better, you don’t know why. The next day, you come and it’s worse. He is dealing with this situation, we are trying to help him.

“The key thing is when he comes back he comes with no pain so he can play as free as possible.”.

What's wrong with Erling Haaland? Man City's superstar has been radiating an air of gloom in front of the cameras - but it's his form on the pitch that should most concern Enzo Maresca, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:22 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 12:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

A smile did eventually spread across the face of Erling Haaland when dissecting Manchester City’s draw with Napoli, stretching their worrying run to one victory in five games.

It has been revealed that not for the first time in recent weeks, he had appeared morose and despondent, radiating an air of gloom, talking about how the team are ‘questioning anything’ amid these results. That’s not exactly inspiring confidence among their supporters.

But just as City’s captain for the night was about to finish his media duties before heading home, one final question focused on Sunday’s clash with Arsenal and a rivalry with a ‘certain centre half’. Haaland’s mood changed instantly.

‘It's always good to play against the best teams,’ mentioned the Norwegian, breaking out into a smirk as he allowed the impending battle with Gabriel to percolate.

‘Arsenal were the best team last year and one of the best in the last five years now, so it's fun to play against them and it’s always fun to play against Gabriel.’.

It has been revealed that there was, at last, some positive emotion. Is Gabriel and that playground scrapping what he needs to re-energise? We’ll find out in a few days.

Erling Haaland appeared morose and despondent following Man City's draw with Napoli, suggesting he was 'questioning everything' amid their worrying run of form.

Haaland did raise a smile about the prospect of his impending battle with Arsenal defender Gabriel this weekend.

The Man City star has shown increasing dejected body language during games and has spent too much time recently with his head bowed and hand waving at team-mates.

Haaland talked about City needing to be at their maximum to take anything from the Emirates this weekend. Whether that is ‘fun’ or not is a different matter entirely, but what Enzo Maresca must demand more from all of his players. Even with 14 goals already this term, that includes Haaland.

According to recent reports, he is leading from the front off the pitch. Standing in front of the cameras more than anyone else, facing up to the dipping form and taking on those responsibilities without complaining. The forward wrote on X on Wednesday afternoon: 'Together through the ups and downs. Thank you for pushing us until the very end yesterday. Full focus on Sunday now.'.

Yet City need more of that leadership between the white lines from somebody who has drawn a blank in four of his last five club matches, despite scoring three times over the international break.

There is too much head bowing and hand waving at the moment.

The 26-year-old admits he has to give extra. And believes that the team are generally creating enough chances for him, even if the freewheeling attacking abandon of early season has vanished.

City's results are clearly affecting Haaland’s mood and that can be self-perpetuating. He admits that failing to reverse this run is hurting him. That is evident by watching his increasingly dejected body language during games and the frustration seen when he gestured at Abdukodir Khusanov as the defender dithered with a routine throw-in during Saturday’s draw against Fulham. It wasn’t the picture of a man happy with his lot.

Industry observers note that only Haaland will know whether that general angst is contributing to a lack of intensity in his own performances. Nobody has mentioned the striker carrying a knock, although Maresca has appeared focused on offering him rest whenever possible over the past three months.

Something is undoubtedly proving an obstacle for him. He’s insisted that it isn’t the guilty verdicts hanging over City and, listening to him, the gripes and disappointment look focused on City’s lack of control in games. It also cannot help that Haaland will feel aggrieved to have seen a goal on Saturday chalked off for a foul on Bernd Leno and then to have not been awarded a penalty for grappling on Tuesday night.

If both or even one of those decisions go his way, the interview that sparked concern with fans – one conducted almost immediately after full time when emotions are at their highest – would likely have been very different.

Industry observers note that city will have to cling on to the idea that a sullen Haaland is at least a Haaland who cares. And a Haaland who cares must surely dig them out of this hole, even if he cannot do that alone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 21:10, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 23:58.

SC Paderborn's clash with visitors Schalke 04 on Saturday at Home Deluxe Arena will be crucial in the Bundesliga's relegation battle.

Sitting 15th with 10 points, the hosts are only above 16th-placed Schalke by three points, and a defeat could leave them as low as 17th by the end of matchweek 11.

The relegation battle looks set to be intense, as while last-placed Borussia Monchengladbach are stranded in 18th, only three points separate 17th from 13th.

Paderborn are one place above the league's relegation playoff spot following their 4-0 loss against Bayer Leverkusen on November 21.

That was their first defeat in five Bundesliga games, though the club drew three times in that period, with their only triumph a 1-0 win against Hamburger SV on October 24.

The hosts have failed to score in three of their last four games in all competitions, and they conceded as many goals in their past two clashes (six) as they had in their prior six contests.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will be pleased by his side's home record given they have won two of their five top-flight fixtures at Home Deluxe Arena while only being beaten twice.

Schalke could view their goalless stalemate with Stuttgart on November 21 positively, especially as it arrested a four-match losing streak.

However, it would be understandable if boss Miron Muslic was feeling pressure given he has failed to oversee a victory in eight games, with his side losing on five occasions.

The visitors might take comfort from the fact they have beaten their hosts in their two most recent meetings, the latest of which was a 3-2 success in the 2. Bundesliga in April 2026.

Die Knappen rank 18th in the division for goals scored (five), though only Borussia Dortmund (seven), Bayern Munich (10) and Freiburg (10) have conceded fewer times (11).

Schalke's form on the road has been poor considering they are winless in their last four away outings, suffering three losses.

SC Paderborn form (all competitions):.

Schalke 04 form (all competitions):.

Paderborn will be unable to call upon defenders Marcel Hoffmeier (muscle) and Nyamekye Awortwie-Grant (ankle), as well as forward Timur Gayret (knee).

Jano ter Horst, Tjark Scheller and Mattes Hansen have been regulars in the backline, and they are set to protect goalkeeper Nahuel Noll.

Stefano Marino and Marvin Pieringer are likely to be trusted as a front two, and they will be keen to improve upon their tallies of two and one league goal respectively.

Schalke's absentee list is extensive, with defender Timo Becker, midfielder Ron Schallenberg and forward Emil Hojlund three of seven injured stars.

Vitalie Becker will start in the backline, Soufian El-Faouzi is likely to anchor the middle of the pitch and Moussa Sylla is certain to lead the frontline.

SC Paderborn possible starting lineup:.

Noll; Ter Horst, Scheller, Hansen; Curda, Baack, Castaneda, Vidovic, Obermair; Marino, Pieringer.

Schalke 04 possible starting lineup:.

Karius; Ebimbe, Katic, Kurucay, Becker; El-Faouzi, Ljubicic; Hwang, Karaman, Aouchiche; Sylla.

While both teams have significantly struggled for results lately, it is impossible for both teams to lose on Saturday.

Perhaps the most likely outcome is a stalemate, especially as neither have proven to be particularly productive in the final third.

Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3392 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has made it abundantly clear that Manchester United target Calvin Bassey will not be leaving Craven Cottage during the January transfer window.

Officially appointed as the upcoming skipper in west London this season, Bassey has been one of Fulham’s key performers and reports over the past fortnight have suggested that new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino has included the 26-year-old on his list of January targets.

Finding a route out of the drop zone and showing some real signs of life on either side of November’s international break, Fulham are unbeaten in each of their previous five consecutive Premier League appearances (two wins, three draws).

Speaking ahead of Fulham’s Premier League showdown against Bournemouth on Sunday, Arbeloa stated unaquivaclay that the Nigerian international is not for sale under any circumstances.

According to recent reports, “Calvin Bassey is not for sale in January. He is a key player for us and there’s no chance for an exit in January. We are working on a new contract”.

With Arbeloa now publicly confirming that the Fulham hierarchy are in active discussions over a new deal for the 49-cap international, Bassey’s current contract contract at Craven Cottage is set to expire next summer.

The Telegraph reported this month that Bassey is attracting plenty of interest from Old Trafford and Manchester United are keen on trying to complete a potential January swoop.

Latest Update: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

Recent findings suggest that it is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very crucial for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra noted.

Industry observers note that elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

The star is also known for speaking out on political issues in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

Recent findings suggest that this reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra remarked. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

Recent findings suggest that "And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

Born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist noted.

In Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

In a recent development, their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more important following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they stated.

It has been revealed that "And I think this is why it's key, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra stated. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

Rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra noted, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

William Saliba is set to make his first-team return for Arsenal in the upcoming matches.

The Frenchman missed the first three months of the season with a back injury that he aggravated at the World Cup in the summer.

Although surgery was not needed, Saliba still required a lengthy period of rest and he is yet to play a single competitive minute for Mikel Arteta’s senior side this season.

He has, however, featured in a couple of behind-closed-doors friendly matches at Arsenal’s training ground. Saliba also played 45 minutes for the Under-21s before the recent international break.

The centre-back was included in the matchday squad against both Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund but remained an unused substitute on each occasion.

Arsenal have a relentless run of fixtures coming up before Christmas, including several huge matches. The Gunners host Manchester City on Sunday as they look to put a nine-point gap between the two clubs in the Premier League title race.

Arteta indicated that Saliba is unlikely to be thrown straight into the starting lineup against City, but could expect to feature very soon.

“Obviously he hasn’t played football for a long, long time,” Arteta said at his pre-match press conference on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that “He can play a certain amount of minutes, so we need to be really, really sure. Especially in that kind of game when he comes in, that he can sustain a certain amount of minutes otherwise we’re not going to have enough subs or opportunities to make those subs.

Industry observers note that “He’s training well, he will have minutes in the next few games. Then he will prove what he’s already done, which is that he’s an unbelievable player.”.

Asked how many minutes Saliba was now capable of playing, Arteta added: “Now he’s got more training, another week or 10 days, that will extend.

“It will depend as well on the type of game and the exposure that he will have throughout the game.”.
