By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 08:02 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 13:10 EST, 25 November 2026.

In September, shortly after pleading guilty to dangerous driving and drug possession, Raheem Sterling shared a statement on social media.

The goal, he implied with a picture of graffiti on a wall, was to 'be better than yesterday' and the intention was to seek 'progress over perfection', as he captioned the image.

But for the former England and Manchester City star to move forward, he has had to fall a long way.

In a recent development, the 31-year-old avoided prison, but was handed a 12-month suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court after he was involved in a dangerous crash in May. Sterling had been driving his £270,000 Lamborghini Urus SUV while under the influence of laughing gas, with multiple motorists spotting him using balloons at the wheel while careening down the M25 and M3 motorways.

During his sentencing hearing, Sterling revealed that he has undergone a 12-day stint in rehab soon after the arrest, after contacting UK addiction services.

According to recent reports, the number of footballers in history who have found themselves entangled with the British justice system is not a small one. But against the backdrop of Sterling's personal story, his fall is a particularly poignant one. The former international built a remarkable career out of a difficult upbringing.

Raheem Sterling has been handed a suspended sentence and 100 hours of community service after being convicted of dangerous driving.

The former Manchester City star has experienced some of the highest heights in professional football - but now languishes without a club.

Sterling lost his father at the age of just two to gun violence, prompting his mother's move from his birthplace of Kingston, Jamaica to the London suburb of Neasden.

Speaking to the Players' Tribune in 2018, Sterling admitted that the tragedy had 'shaped his entire life'.

'For a few years, we lived with our grandmother in Kingston, and I remember watching the other kids with their mums and just feeling really jealous,' he revealed. 'I didn't fully understand what my mum was doing for us. I just knew that she was gone. My grandma was amazing, but everybody wants their mum at that age.'.

According to recent reports, his father's shocking death also inspired a gun tattoo inked on his leg above his right 'shooting' foot, there as part of a promise he had made that he 'would never touch a gun in his lifetime'. Although the tattoo prompted criticism from anti-gun campaigners in 2018, Sterling was adamant that his message was aligned with theirs, with the player backed by the FA.

It has been revealed that after moving to England, his mother Nadine found work as a cleaner. Sterling and his siblings would sometimes help her during her early morning shifts cleaning hotels at 5am before their school day started. With rent a continual challenge for the family as money was tight, they moved house often.

But Sterling's prodigious talent on the football pitch was breaking through, with the winger asked to join Queens Park Rangers' youth set-up at just 10 years old.

Sacrifices were made to allow for this: in 2021, Sterling released a custom football boot with New Balance paying tribute to the three buses - the 18, the 182 and 140 - he had to catch to make the return journey from home near Wembley to the west London training ground, accompanied by his older sister Lakima.

'The red double-deckers with the blue wool '80s vibe on the seats,' he reminisced. 'Spent ages on those. We'd leave at 3.15 and get home at 11 pm. Every. Single. Day.

Sources indicate that 'She'd sit upstairs in the little cafe and chill until I was done with training. Imagine being 17 years old and doing that for your little brother. And I never once heard her say, 'Nah, I don't wanna take him.'.

As a youngster, Sterling's footballing talent was prodigious and helped him sign with QPR at the age of 10.

Five years later and Sterling had parlayed this into a move to Liverpool's academy, with the star breaking through to the first team in 2012.

'At the time, I didn't understand how much she was sacrificing. Her and my mum got me here. My whole family played a massive part in my life. Without them, you wouldn't even know me.'.

Football was a necessary focus as well as passion, with Sterling once removed from mainstream education as a youngster and sent to Vernon House, an adapted school to help with behavioral problems.

His teacher there, Chris Beschi, told the Guardian in 2018 that he had noted to a young Sterling: 'If you carry on the way you're going, by the time you're 17 you'll either be playing for England or you'll be in prison.'.

But Beschi was able to see a different side to Sterling too, describing the boy as having 'a kind and innocent passion about him', and as football took over, Premier League rivals clamoured to sign him up to their youth ranks.

Nadine was adamant that he should be developed outside of London to avoid any possibility of getting caught up in gang violence, and Chelsea and Arsenal's loss was Liverpool's gain, with Sterling joining the academy at the age of 15 for a then punchy fee of £500,000.

After that, Sterling's career rapidly gathered momentum. With the arrival of Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish in the dugout in early 2011, Sterling was moved into the Europa League squad, fast-tracking integration with established first-team stars. Playing and travel time was limited, however.

Industry observers note that just over a year later, and the player was readied for his first senior start against Wigan Athletic, at the tender age of 17 years and 107 days. The following season saw him named as the club's Young Player of the Year and shortlisted for the PFA Young Player of the Year. By 2014, he was winning the Golden Boy award, and becoming the most expensive English footballer to date with his £49million move to Man City.

It has been revealed that but against the backdrop of success on the football pitch, there were challenging moments away from it. In 2013, Sterling was accused of two separate counts of assault, one against a former girlfriend and another against a different woman. He was found not guilty of the former, with the latter incident dropped after a witness failed to attend court.

Two years later, in March 2015, Sterling was snapped by tabloids reportedly smoking from a shisha pipe. And, in a moment that spoke of what was to come, it was alleged that he might have also been using nitrous oxide for recreational purposes. Manager Brendan Rodgers was keen to protect Sterling and urged people to remember: 'Young players make mistakes.'.

Sterling had an uneven stint at Liverpool but put on display enough of his talent to earn him the 2014 Golden Boy award.

His spell on Merseyside also secured him entrance into the England squad, where he became one of the standouts of the 2010s.

Shortly before his move to Man City Sterling started dating Paige Milian, now his long-term partner and mother of his children (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

The clean slate offered by Man City might have itself been appealing. Things had become somewhat tricky at Anfield, after Sterling had refused a new deal, with the player booed while on duty for England under then-manager Roy Hodgson. Rodgers and Sterling rowed publicly in the media over suggestions that he had turned down a new contract for financial reasons, and his move to the Etihad came after club legends including Steven Gerrard, Jamie Carragher and Graeme Souness had all criticised his conduct.

The first season at the Etihad might have been a false start, with Sterling notably injured in March leading to the premature curtailing of his campaign, but under incoming manager Pep Guardiola, Sterling began flying. At the same time, he was underscoring his importance for England under Hodgson, and then Gareth Southgate.

Recent findings suggest that 'In terms of, "Can he fulfil it?", he'll give himself every chance,' Southgate said when asked if he thought Sterling might win the Ballon d'Or after victory against Kosovo in 2019. 'There are some outstanding players around - (Eden) Hazard, (Kevin) De Bruyne, Messi, Ronaldo.

'But he (Sterling) has got the drive, he's got the professionalism, he's got the ability. He's physically and mentally strong for such a small-statured lad.'.

And against the backdrop of his growth on the pitch, Sterling was becoming an notable voice away from it too, frequently speaking out against the racism young black players were targeted with, and from personal experience. In 2017, Sterling was attacked outside Man City's training ground by a convicted football hooligan hurling racist language at him. In 2018, he suffered racist abuse on the pitch while featuring for Man City against Chelsea.

396 Premier League appearances, 123 goals.

1 PFA Young Player Of The Season.

GQ magazine described Sterling as football's 'most influential player' in 2019 in recognition of his climb to the very top of the game, and for his increasingly high profile as a campaigner off the pitch.

Sterling branded negative tabloid coverage as racist, and made an address to the United Nations.

In a recent development, 'Discrimination is discrimination. It doesn't matter if it's your sexuality, or your color, you shouldn't (discriminate) at all', Sterling remarked, speaking to the UN Human Rights Office for the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination. 'We need – as a collective – to take responsibility. This is a new age where color can't define who you are'.

It has been revealed that sterling also established the Raheem Sterling Foundation in 2021, which the footballer funds and which helps to support youth education projects, including fighting knife crime and helping children out of poverty. That year, he was awarded an MBE for services to racial equality in sport.

As his public profile hit fresh heights, Sterling kept scoring, becoming Man City's seventh-highest goalscorer of all time. But limited game time under Guardiola led to a move to Chelsea for £47.5m, and on a salary worth an eye-watering £325,000 per week.

Sterling was a focal point of the Man City team which achieved a staggering trophy haul in the late 2010s.

His move to Chelsea in 2022 set him up to be one of the stars of the club's new era under BlueCo but he failed to hit the right notes across two personally underwhelming seasons.

After an abortive loan move to Arsenal, Sterling signed for Feyenoord at the start of the year but did not see his deal extended past the end of the season.

Recent findings suggest that in what might be seen as the beginning of the end, his first season in Chelsea blue failed to hit the heights required. There was chaos in west London as the club cycled through Thomas Tuchel, Graham Potter, Bruno Saltor and Frank Lampard in the dugout but Sterling still bagged nine goals and a further four assists in his 38 appearances, as well as securing a place in Southgate's World Cup squad that year.

Industry observers note that sterling made an impact in the group stages in Qatar, but was forced home after his family home was burgled. While his long-term partner Paige Milian and three children were not at the property, Sterling was shaken and flew back to Oxshott from the camp before returning in time for the quarter-final against France.

While his first season with Chelsea had room for improvement at Stamford Bridge, his second was even limper. The latest manager on the club's merry-go-round, Enzo Maresca, remarked in August 2024 that he was going to 'struggle' for minutes, effectively frozen out.

According to recent reports, from there, his on-pitch decline was swift. An abortive loan across the city to Arsenal had the promise of a step up, but Sterling struggled just as hard for game time. A difficult time was compounded by a second break-in at his home, with the family forced to escape but luckily unharmed.

On his return to Chelsea, Maresca placed him in the now-infamous bomb squad, forced to train away from the first-team players, share separate, smaller locker rooms, and all but ostracised within Cobham.

Offers swirled around Sterling as they have done for all his decorated career, but the possibility of a move to Bayer Leverkusen or Juventus did not go much further than exploratory talks. A switch to nearby Fulham fell through. With money far from a motivating factor, the winger opted not to accept a lucrative contract and move to Saudi Arabia.

Instead, Sterling stayed out of the game until his contract was mutually terminated in January of this year.

Hopes of finding that at his next club Feyenoord evaporated on his debut. Signed until the end of the 2025-26 season, Sterling stepped onto the pitch in February after nine months out and looked rusty.

Recent findings suggest that the critics were brutal, but head coach Robin van Persie did his best to defend his fresh player. It was too harsh to judge him over just six or eight weeks, he stressed.

Within weeks, he was back in the UK, with his arrest coming in May. Any offers that might have come his way over the summer have subsequently dried up.

Sterling crashed his £270,000 Lambourghini Urus while driving under the influence.

The arrest took place shortly after his time in Rotterdam came to an end, with the star pleading guilty in September.

Since the arrest, Sterling has been keeping a low profile and focusing on his family (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

With offers from football clubs quieter, the winger has focused on other ventures including his Playmaker Films (Source: Instagram/Raheem Sterling).

Sterling has since worked on his Playmaker Films, a content agency, and launched 'The Cage', a grassroots football competition where teams of four face off for eight minutes with £5,000 on the line.

In a recent development, 'Football's about expressing yourself,' he remarked when interviewed about why he created the contest, which showcases individuality on caged pitches similar to ones he would have learned to play on. 'The game is a beautiful thing'.

It has been revealed that sterling's story is of a remarkable rise from adversity to the highest levels in professional sport. His private life has clearly been complicated - District Judge Kirsty Allman revealed his drug problem had 'become a maladaptive coping mechanism during a difficult period in his career'.

Any way back seems a long way off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 23:15, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 23:57.

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo could return to first-team action before Christmas.

Dasilva has been out of action since sustaining a hamstring injury while playing for Brentford’s B team in a Premier League Cup game against Wycombe Wanderers Under-21s in August.

Milambo, meanwhile, has not played first-team football since sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury while representing the Netherlands Under-21s in October 2025.

Dasilva and Milambo stepped up their recoveries with valuable minutes in Brentford B’s 2-1 win over Hull City on Sunday, with the latter scoring the opening goal at Wheatsheaf Park.

While the pair remain unavailable for Saturday’s Premier League clash against Manchester United, Andrews was able to offer a positive patch when asked whether the duo could return before Christmas.

“Yeah, that would certainly be the plan,” Andrews told reporters in Thursday’s pre-match press conference.

“We have a few games before then. They played 45 minutes the other night in the B team game. They both played well and came through the game well.

According to recent reports, “They’re building the fitness level that’s needed to come into the first-team space, but they’re training with us pretty consistently. They’ve been in and out to be ready for the B team game.

“They’ll continue that over the next week or two and then hopefully they can gatecrash the first-team squad.”.

In regard to other absentees, Brentford are unable to call upon the injured quartet of Nathan Collins, Aaron Hickey, Rico Henry and Kaye Furo.

Meanwhile, striker Igor Thiago will serve the second game of a three-match ban after being sent off in the defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion earlier this month.

Those available will be looking to build on Brentford’s impressive 4-0 win over Everton at the Gtech Community Stadium on Monday, which lifted the club up to sixth spot in the Premier League table.

#220928. What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

What the Democrats' midterms win means for the US economy and Trump

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1067 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one glitch ranked above all others: the economy.
  • So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?
  • Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the millions who cast their ballots in the US midterm elections, one glitch ranked above all others: the economy.

So what does the Democrats' stunning capture of both the US Senate and House of Representatives mean for the economy and economic policy, given that President Donald Trump still has two years of his term to go?

Markets have rebounded after initially trending negatively. Global stocks rallied as investors appeared to take heart from the Democrats' victory.

According to recent reports, with Democrats now holding comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress and Trump still in the White House, it could lead to gridlock in Washington. Trump has already said he would become "Mr Veto," meaning he would block any legislation the Democrats advance.

"The magnitude of the gains for the Democrats in the midterms does not change too much for the near-term policy outlook, given the party still lacks a filibuster-proof majority in the Senate and President Trump has veto power to block legislation," Stephen Brown, chief North America economist with Capital Economics, mentioned in a note.

It has been revealed that "I think we are looking at two years of complete 100% gridlock," Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, nonresident senior fellow with the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told DW after the results came in. "Nothing will get done of any kind.".

Some investors appear worried that the Democrats could force through AI regulation, especially if they also win the White House in 2028. Rising opposition among large majorities of the US population to data centers — the key infrastructure behind AI — helped secure victories for many Democratic candidates.

Kirkegaard, who is also a senior fellow at Bruegel, a European economics think tank, mentioned the vote showed the extent of that opposition. Even if the Democrats can't force regulation, he thinks local opposition will make it harder for data centers to be built, which could hit the valuation of big tech firms that have benefitted from the AI boom.

"This election reveals that the political underpinning of the rapid, aggressive AI growth story is shaky," he noted. "It doesn't mean it's going to stop or be made illegal, but the dynamic of the growth story has shifted.".

In a recent development, if the Democrats were to win the presidency in 2028, Brown said, they would be perfectly placed to make major policy changes. "That includes the potential for tax hikes on corporations and high-income individuals as well as regulation that could delay the AI rollout," he said.

According to polling conducted in early October by the Pew Research Center, 56% of Americans say Trump's tariff policies will have mostly negative impacts on the country, with only 20% saying mostly positive.

Recent findings suggest that that sentiment clearly drove many Democrats to victory in the midterms — particularly in states where tariffs have had a particularly negative impact. That includes those with sectors reliant on exports, such as Texas, Michigan, Iowa and Illinois, where counter-tariffs have hit and those that have high trade volumes with Canada.

Yet, barring an unprecedented climbdown from Trump — who has been ideologically wedded to tariffs since he first became a public figure almost 50 years ago — it's not clear how the Democrats could force substantial change to the president's signature economic policy.

According to recent reports, "Trump will not be moderated," Deborah Elms, head of trade policy at the Hinrich Foundation in Singapore, told DW earlier this year. "Expect him to continue his trade disruption and tariff policies for as long as he remains in the Oval Office.".

Though the US Constitution gives Congress the power to collect and organize tariffs, various laws passed over the years have given presidents power to implement tariffs when they cite certain conditions, such as national security or economic emergencies.

It has been revealed that trump has already used such avenues for his tariffs and can continue to do so, despite some legal rebukes. However, while Congress can't necessarily force an end to Trump's existing tariffs, it can now take further legal action against them to prevent greater escalation.

Though Trump and the Democrats are clearly not going to make common cause, Kirkegaard remarked, the scale of the Republicans' defeat might force Trump to be less erratic in his policymaking, from escalating his trade war with Canada to his Iran policy.

Trump noted in the aftermath of Tuesday's defeats that he would "work with" the Democrats and told the Financial Times in the run-up to the vote that he was unlikely to escalate the war in Iran.

Were a deal to be struck with Iran, soaring energy prices — a pivotal election problem — could finally fall, helping voters with their cost-of-living concerns.

Industry observers note that "You've got to get a deal with Iran, and you've got to bring down gas prices," Kirkegaard said. "From a political point of view, that's the most vital thing now.".

George Saravelos, an analyst with Deutsche Bank FX Research, thinks the markets are beginning to become more optimistic in that area. "With oil flows through the Middle East having materially recovered, the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium of re-escalation and energy supply disruption," he noted in a note.

Despite the scale of the Democrats' victory, the fact that Trump remains in the Oval Office will complicate all efforts to force a change to signature economic policies and challenges.

Yet Congress can now exert considerable pressure. Another problem vital to voters was corruption and the belief that the Trump administration has engaged in corruption and personal enrichment while in office.

That raises the prospect of the latest Democratic-controlled Congress launching legal investigations and potentially pursuing another impeachment of Trump, which could force the president to negotiate on some economic issues to secure his political survival.

"Can you find 10 or 12 Republican senators who, in the face of overwhelming corruption, would be willing to vote for articles of impeachment? I wouldn't rule it out," Kirkegaard noted. "And that's a scenario in which Trump might suddenly be much more accommodating to, for instance, abandoning most of his tariffs.".

Despite voters' clear rejection of Trump's economic policies, the Democratic Party's newly minted senators, congressmen and congresswomen face an uphill battle in trying to reverse them.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

And that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

Recent findings suggest that in that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer remarked he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain remarked.

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick stated he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick remarked before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

Recent findings suggest that “But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Absolutely tipping it down in Como, with 64mm of rain forecast before #MUFC kick-off here tomorrow ☔️ https://t.co/WvI3X8dilh.

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 23:19, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:12.

Bayern Munich will hope to arrest their troubles by getting the better of hosts Hamburger SV at Volksparkstadion on Saturday and reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga table.

The Bavarians are second with 22 points in the league, so they will need Borussia Dortmund to avoid winning in order to climb to first, whereas the home side are 12th with 12 points.

Hamburger's campaign has been positive, especially as they have taken three more points after 10 matchweeks this season than they did at the same stage in 2025-26.

The club did lose 4-0 against Werder Bremen on November 22, and a defeat on the weekend could leave them just two points above the bottom three.

Head coach Daniel Thioune will be alarmed that his side have lost four of their last five games in all competitions, with the club scoring five goals while conceding on 12 occasions.

The Green-Whites' next task is to get the better of Bayern for the first time since July 2011, a period in which they suffered 17 defeats and drew three times.

HSV's record as hosts has been commendable this term considering they have triumphed in three of their five league outings at Volksparkstadion, though they were beaten twice in that stretch.

Bayern are in the unusual position of having to bounce back from a loss after Lille won 2-1 against them in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That was Vincent Kompany's second game on the touchline following his collapse in October, but his first match back was hardly better, with his side drawing 1-1 with FC Koln on November 20.

The visitors are only two points behind first-placed Borussia Dortmund, but with numerous injuries throughout the squad, there are fears that the gap could widen.

Injuries and form are not the only problems plaguing the champions, whose hierarchy have come under fire for their handling of Jamal Musiala's health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to speak up in support of the attacker.

Nevertheless, it should not be forgotten that the Bavarians have scored 30 goals in 10 top-flight games, while only Dortmund have conceded fewer goals than their 10.

Bayern's defeat against Lille was their first in any competition this campaign, and it was also their first away defeat, with the visitors having won six and drawn three of their first nine away fixtures of the season.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Bayern Munich form (all competitions):.

Hamburger midfielder Nicolai Remberg has been ruled out for the rest of the season, meaning the hosts may have to rely upon Nicolas Capaldo in the middle of the pitch.

With striker Yussuf Poulsen unavailable, Patson Daka will be expected to lead the line, and he may be supported by Fabio Vieira.

Bayern will be without Harry Kane for months due to an ankle injury, and to make matters worse, Michael Olise is a doubt.

Luis Diaz should be ready to feature in some capacity on the weekend, though he faces the prospect of playing in a forward line led by natural midfielder Konrad Laimer.

Aleksandar Pavlovic played in an advanced role against Lille due to injuries in attack, but he should be able to return to a deeper role alongside Kimmich.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Fernandes; Nandja, Bornauw, Omari; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Capaldo, Gronbaek, Wolfe; Daka, Vieira.

Bayern Munich possible starting lineup:.

Urbig; Stanisic, Upamecano, Tah, Ito; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Diaz, Karl, Brown; Laimer.

Hamburger may never have a better opportunity than now to take points from Bayern, who have several key absentees.

However, Bayern still boast immense quality in their squad, and they should still be able to come out on top, even if the match is far from straightforward.

European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.
  • Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.
  • The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.

European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.

Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

In a recent development, tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.

Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Tech giant (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.

Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.

Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending plans and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.

"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and Fresh Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

In a recent development, "Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he mentioned. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.".

  • Excelsior and Telstar drew 2-2 at BUKO Stadion on November 1, 2025 and again at Stadion Woudestein on January 17, 2026, but the Kralingers now sit 13th on 14 points, four clear of the relegation play-off place that De Witte Leeuwen occupy on 10.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 26 Nov 2026 23:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:10.

SBV Excelsior host SC Telstar at Stadion Woudestein in Rotterdam in round 14 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday with kick-off at 3.30pm GMT.

Excelsior and Telstar drew 2-2 at BUKO Stadion on November 1, 2025 and again at Stadion Woudestein on January 17, 2026, but the Kralingers now sit 13th on 14 points, four clear of the relegation play-off place that De Witte Leeuwen occupy on 10.

Ruben den Uil's Excelsior ended a run of five straight league defeats with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on November 21, their first league victory at De Kuip since 1980.

After Givairo Read gave Feyenoord a lead on two minutes, Mario Dominguez levelled on six, Irakli Yegoian scored a penalty on 40 and Casper Widell headed in from a corner on 58.

Jan Plug, who is on loan from Feyenoord, turned the ball into his own net on 67 minutes, but the visitors held on.

Excelsior had 10 points from their first five games, including a 4-0 win at Cambuur on the opening day, then took one point from the next seven.

The low point came on November 1, when Twente won 9-0 at Woudestein, the heaviest league defeat in the club's history, with Nesto Groen sent off after five minutes.

A 1-0 home loss to Go Ahead Eagles on November 7 left Excelsior without a league goal in four games, and they had conceded 20 times in five league matches before the Feyenoord win, leaving a goal difference of -12 from 13 games.

Henk Brugge, in his first permanent head coach job after succeeding Anthony Correia in May, has Telstar 16th on the Eredivisie table with 10 points from two wins, four draws and seven defeats, with 19 goals scored and 28 conceded.

Telstar went ahead after 16 minutes against PEC Zwolle on November 21 through a Simon Graves own goal, but Dylan Mbayo scored twice before half time and Ibrahim Cissoko added a third after a poor back pass from Gabi Caschili.

That 3-1 home defeat means Telstar have gone 17 matches without beating Zwolle in all competitions, and Brugge admitted afterwards that his side may have played the better football but defended badly at key moments.

Telstar have scored in each of their last six league games, 14 goals in all, but they conceded 16 across those matches, including a 4-2 win over Utrecht and 2-2 draws with ADO Den Haag and at Fortuna Sittard.

The defence is the problem at BUKO Stadion, where Telstar have conceded 20 goals in seven league games this season.

Away from Velsen-Zuid, Telstar have taken one point from their last three league trips, losing 1-0 at AZ Alkmaar and 3-2 at Go Ahead Eagles before the 2-2 draw at Fortuna Sittard, and Tyrone Owusu leads the team with five goals this season.

SBV Excelsior form (all competitions):.

Telstar form (all competitions):.

Excelsior have no reported injuries or suspensions, with Groen available again after serving his ban by missing the Go Ahead Eagles game and the trip to Feyenoord.

Sliti, who has three league goals, feared a bruised or broken thumb after Netherlands Under-21s duty on November 17 but started at De Kuip, so Alireza Jahanbakhsh and David Garden remain options from the bench.

Noah Naujoks is back in the midfield after a long injury absence and started alongside Lennard Hartjes, who has suffered three cruciate ligament tears in his career, two of them at Excelsior.

Telstar have no confirmed absentees, with Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes both returning from injury as substitutes against Zwolle, on 57 and 84 minutes respectively.

Nokkvi Thorisson and Jeff Hardeveld, who both came on after 57 minutes against Zwolle, are options to start in attack.

SBV Excelsior possible starting lineup:.

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Naujoks, Hartjes, Yegoian; Sliti, Dominguez, Thorsteinsson.

Telstar possible starting lineup:.

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Martha, Owusu, Demircan; Brouwer.

Excelsior highlighted at Feyenoord that the goals have returned, with a side that had scored once in five league games finding the net three times against the division's second-highest scoring attack, including a Widell header from a corner and a Dominguez finish after a midfield giveaway.

Telstar have scored in six straight league games, so a clean sheet is unlikely for an Excelsior defence that has conceded 31 times in 13 matches, but Telstar have taken one point from their last three away games and let in 20 goals in seven home league games, which suggests their backline will struggle with Dominguez and Sliti.

The counter-argument is the 9-0 Twente result, yet that came with Groen sent off after five minutes, while the draws in both meetings last season show Telstar can score at Woudestein, so Excelsior should edge a match in which both sides concede.

Latest Update: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 80 min read (16047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~80 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering.
  • Recent findings suggest that A long-standing challenge in genome engineering is how to achieve precise, programmable integration of large (≥1 kb) DNA cargo.
  • Recent findings suggest that a, Transposon organization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

Recent findings suggest that A long-standing challenge in genome engineering is how to achieve precise, programmable integration of large (≥1 kb) DNA cargo. CRISPR–Cas nucleases are capable of efficient DNA cleavage3, but their reliance on host DNA repair pathways limits both the efficiency and fidelity of large insertions4. CASTs offer an alternative strategy by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration, without the need for DNA double-strand breaks or homologous recombination1,2. CASTs evolved from Tn7-like transposons through the acquisition of a CRISPR effector, with distinct effectors defining each of the major subfamilies: type V-K, I-F3, I-B and I-D5. All CASTs encode a conserved set of proteins: TniQ (bridging protein), TnsC (AAA+ regulator) and TnsA–TnsB (TnsA/B, transposase complex) (Fig. 1a). The CRISPR effector and TniQ form the targeting module, and TnsA/B and TnsC form the transposition machinery (Fig. 1a). Although all CASTs perform RNA-guided transposition, they can display a remarkable diversity of targeting behaviours. For example, in type I-B2 CASTs, the transposition machinery can associate with either the sequence-specific DNA-binding protein TnsD or an RNA-guided targeting complex6. Type V-K CASTs exhibit a robust off-target pathway, driven by the propensity of TniQ and TnsC to load at non-cognate sites7. Type I-F3 CASTs have a Cascade effector and exhibit near-exclusive on-target integration8, which makes them of particular interest for clinical9 and microbial genome-editing applications10.

Recent findings suggest that a, Transposon organization. R and L, right and left transposon ends. Parallel lines indicate discontinuity. b, Dual screen of TnsA designs: activity and specificity scores are plotted relative to wild type (normalized to 0,0), with density plots on the top and right. The red circle represents the top design, D1A. c, In vivo integration activity of VchCAST. The graph demonstrates individual data points. Data are mean ± s.d. from biological triplicates. Ara, arabinose selection; Kan, kanamycin selection. d, In vivo genome-wide insertion profile. Red arrow indicates target site. e, Close-up view of target site in d with insertion window. f, Cryo-EM density map (2.9 Å) of the class 1 STC at 0.129 threshold. Proteins coloured as in a. Target-site duplication is shown in red. g, Top, atomic model of the STC oriented as in f. Black symbols (asterisk, star and diamond) indicate regions shown in h–k. Bottom, domain organization of TnsB. Striped regions represent disordered N- and C-terminal tails. CD, catalytic domain; DBD, DNA-binding domain. h, Overlay of the catalytic TnsB in STC assembly class 2 (white) and class 1 (purple) shows conformational changes involved in transition from class 2 to class 1, with the catalytic domain and TBD rotating as indicated. View rotated 90° relative to g. i, Class 2 model shown in the same orientation as in g. Catalytic residues D223, D308 and E344 are shown as sticks; dashed lines indicate unresolved positions (331–341). j, Same as i, for the class 1 model. Magnesium ions are shown as green spheres. k, Close-up view of the region marked by the diamond and asterisk in g, rotated by 10°.

Recent structural studies of CAST assemblies have begun to reveal how this conserved transposition machinery accommodates architecturally diverse CRISPR effectors. The V-K system from Scytonema hofmannii, ShCAST, is the best characterized to date; its holo integration complex (HIC) structure demonstrates that the host factor S15 and TniQ associate with Cas12k and together strongly distort target DNA, an event that is required to recruit two helical turns of hexameric TnsC11,12, which in turn engages the transposase TnsB via its C-terminal hook13. A complete TnsABCD integration complex structure exists for type I-B2 CAST14, but structural information on other CAST assemblies is limited to isolated components or subcomplexes. TnsC organization is not fixed across CAST systems, as it forms a heptameric ring in other CAST systems, including I-F315 and I-B216, as well as in Tn717. Whether mechanistic insights from one system can be extended to other CAST systems is unclear.

Despite extensive biochemical, genetic and structural studies of individual components, the mechanisms by which type I-F3 CASTs achieve precise on-target integration remain unknown. Chromatin immunoprecipitation with sequencing (ChIP–seq) experiments have revealed a hierarchical assembly pathway in which Cascade–TniQ occupancy precedes TnsC recruitment, and stable TnsC accumulation depends on the transposase TnsA/B15. Cascade–TniQ binds DNA promiscuously and forms partial R-loops at many candidate sites15, but they cannot complete R-loop formation on their own18, suggesting that additional steps are required to license TnsC recruitment. Structures of TnsC15 have established the molecular details of its homo-oligomerization on DNA. Nonetheless, how all these components come together to form an integration-competent complex at the RNA-guided target site remains unknown. Thus, a structure of the fully assembled HIC is critical to establish the mechanistic basis for RNA-guided DNA integration and for rational engineering efforts to improve type I-F3 CAST integration efficiency for translational applications9,19.

Sources indicate that here, using a combination of computational protein design, single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and directed in vivo mutagenesis, we uncover the mechanisms that regulate HIC assembly in the type I-F3 VchCAST system. The architectures of the strand-transfer complex (STC) and the full HIC reveal how RNA-guided target recognition, TnsC oligomerization and TnsA/B recruitment converge to organize a stable integration complex. Despite large structural differences across type V-K, I-F3 and I-B2 CASTs, conserved local features suggest universal mechanistic principles of RNA-guided DNA integration across CASTs. Our results reveal a context-dependent structural mechanism, whereby each of the aforementioned components undergoes significant conformational rearrangements relative to their isolated structures15,18,20 as a means to license RNA-guided integration complex assembly. Our work also demonstrates how structure-guided computational protein design can be leveraged as a highly effective strategy for improving integration activity without compromising specificity.

Industry observers note that because TnsA was refractory to purification (Methods), we hypothesized that stabilizing it in a product-bound conformation could both enhance activity and facilitate structure determination. We therefore modelled the VchCAST STC (comprising TnsA, TnsB and a strand-transfer DNA substrate) using AlphaFold 321 (Extended Data Fig. 1). We then redesigned the TnsA sequence using LigandMPNN22, with functionally important residues held fixed (32%; 74 out of 230 residues; Supplementary Fig. 1) and applied per-residue sampling biased towards TnsA homologues. Designs were grouped by sequence divergence from wild-type TnsA (TnsAWT), then selected for experimental screening on the basis of predicted confidence scores (Methods).

We screened 500 top-ranking designs, each containing between 2 and 87 substitutions (Supplementary Table 1), using our previously developed high-throughput Escherichia coli screen23. In brief, a kanamycin resistance cassette serves as the donor DNA, such that kanamycin selection reports overall integration activity. On-target genomic integration is enriched by dual kanamycin and arabinose selection, which selects for disruption of an arabinose-inducible ccdB toxin gene. Activity and specificity scores are calculated as the log2-transformed fold change in variant frequency compared to wild type23. Of the 500 designs tested, 67% showed higher activity than TnsAWT (Fig. 1b). The top-performing design (D1A; Fig. 1b) incorporates 27 mutations (Extended Data Fig. 2) and has a log2-transformed activity score of 6.37, with no significant change in specificity (specificity score = −0.27; Fig. 1b). This improvement translates in vivo to an approximately 100-fold increase in integration activity relative to TnsAWT (Fig. 1c) while maintaining high fidelity, with 98% of insertions occurring on target (Fig. 1d) and at the expected distance, 82 base pairs (bp) from the protospacer adjacent motif (PAM)1 (Fig. 1e).

TnsA is required for transposition, but its catalytic activity determines product identity: cleavage of the 5′ donor end generates simple insertions, whereas a failure to cleave generates co-integrates24. Long-read sequencing distinguishes these two products, establishing the extent of TnsA activity8. Using long-read sequencing, we found that D1A produced more co-integrates than wild-type TnsA (42% simple insertions versus 96.2%; Extended Data Fig. 3). This phenotype was attributable primarily to the Q73K substitution: reverting Q73 to the wild-type residue restored simple insertion frequency to near wild-type levels (92.4%) without compromising the transposition activity gains conferred by the broader D1A redesign (Extended Data Fig. 3), indicating that Q73K governs the simple insertion/co-integrate balance independently of those gains. This also does not appear to be a general consequence of the design campaign, as other top-scoring designs retain full catalytic activity (97–100% simple insertions; Extended Data Fig. 3). Finally, we examined the effect of redesign on the folded state of TnsA. Circular dichroism analysis revealed that TnsAWT has substantial random coil content, consistent with an unfolded protein, whereas D1A has a spectrum consistent with a well-folded, mostly α-helical protein (Supplementary Fig. 2). Together, these results demonstrate that zero-shot structure-based computational design can both improve CAST activity and facilitate structure determination, creating a framework for iterative structure-guided optimization.

Sources indicate that we next determined the cryo-EM structure of the STC containing integration host factor (IHF), D1A (hereafter referred to as TnsA), TnsB and a strand-transfer DNA substrate (2.9 Å overall resolution; Fig. 1f,g and Supplementary Figs. 3 and 4). We found that K73 occupies a second-shell position relative to the TnsA active site, sufficiently close to form a hydrogen bond with catalytic residues, providing a likely explanation for why the Q73K substitution reduces the catalytic activity of TnsA (Supplementary Fig. 5). As this perturbation is confined to the local active site environment, the D1A structure presented here should therefore represent an otherwise catalytically competent state. IHF promotes CAST transposition 10-fold, although it is not absolutely required for activity25. In our structure, IHF binds LE DNA at a site between LE1 and LE2 (Supplementary Fig. 3), bending the DNA to permit occupancy of additional TnsB binding sites. This binding mode has been described in molecular detail in a related study that lacked TnsA and other components of the HIC20. Here, we instead focus on the novel insights we observe in the presence of the partner protein TnsA.

TnsA localizes to the 5′ end of the donor DNA, where it binds the flanking host DNA and forms a continuous β-sheet with TnsB, a feature highly similar to previous TnsA structures from the type I-B2 PmcCAST system (Supplementary Fig. 6). We also identified conformational flexibility in the STC ensemble, which was separable by 3D classification. The highest-resolution class, containing the majority of particles, corresponds to class 1 (Supplementary Fig. 7a), whereas a second, minor 3D class (27% of particles, 3.2 Å overall resolution) lacks observable density for target DNA and for TnsB beyond the C-terminal helix (CTH) domain (class 2; Supplementary Fig. 7b,c and Extended Data Table 1). Closer inspection of class 2 reveals that the catalytic DDE triad (D223, D308, and E344) is too distant (6.2–6.9 Å; Supplementary Fig. 8) to form a functional active site, and that the loop preceding E344 (residues 331–341) is disordered (Fig. 1i). By contrast, class 1 has the expected arrangement of catalytic residues, as well as two magnesium ions: a catalytic magnesium with the expected coordination geometry and a second structural magnesium positioned nearby that stabilizes a sharp bend at the target–donor DNA junction (Fig. 1j). The conformational transition from class 2 to class 1 would entail a ~20° rotation of the catalytic domain and target DNA-binding domain (TBD) of TnsB at the TnsA–TnsB interface (blue star, Fig. 1h), reorienting these domains to engage target DNA. Concurrently, a target DNA-binding loop in the catalytic domain of TnsB (residues 359–378) becomes structured, further priming the complex for target DNA binding (Fig. 1k). These structural observations show that the STC exhibits conformational heterogeneity; one conformation (class 2) appearing catalytically inactive, and the other (class 1) showing rearrangements consistent with active site organization and target DNA engagement. As TnsA/B requires additional transposon-encoded partner proteins (that is, TnsC) for integration activity1, these conformational changes may reflect a mechanism of activation for TnsA/B.

We next determined the cryo-EM structure of the HIC, comprising Cascade–TniQ, TnsA, TnsB and TnsC, assembled on a strand-transfer DNA substrate that mimics the in vivo integration product (Supplementary Fig. 3). Our cryo-EM data analysis reveals substantial compositional heterogeneity, with three identifiable assemblies (Extended Data Fig. 4): Cascade–TniQ (target-recognition complex (TRC); 3 Å overall resolution), STC–TnsC (4.3 Å overall resolution) and the HIC (4.5 Å overall resolution; Fig. 2a). In the HIC, local resolution is highest at the Cascade core (3.7 Å) and decreases towards the STC periphery (about 7 Å; Extended Data Table 1 and Supplementary Fig. 9). Although IHF was included in the reconstitution, we did not observe IHF bound in the resulting structure, which may be attributable to the sample preparation method (Methods). Notably, the overall map was of sufficient quality to interpret different structural features without the need of a composite map stitched from subtracted focused-refined regions.

In a recent development, a, Cryo-EM density map of the HIC at 4.5 Å resolution, displayed at a threshold of 0.077, showing all components required for integration complex assembly. The HIC contains a Cascade effector, a TniQ dimer, a heptameric TnsC ring, a TnsB tetramer and two copies of TnsA (Fig. 2b), consistent with the stoichiometry established by structures of individual subcomplexes15,18,20. However, density for the seventh TnsC protomer (TnsC7) is noticeably weaker than for the other subunits (Supplementary Fig. 10), indicating substoichiometric occupancy or flexibility. The DNA-binding footprint accounts for the characteristic 82 bp integration distance from the PAM: 32 nucleotides occupied by the guide RNA spacer, followed by a 21, 14 and 15 bp footprint corresponding to TniQ, TnsC and TnsB, respectively, and terminating in a 5-nucleotide target-site duplication (Fig. 2c). Mutagenesis of the Cas8/5 PAM-interacting residues S127, R243, N246 and D461 substantially reduces integration activity (Supplementary Fig. 11), consistent with an notable role for these residues in PAM recognition and transposition. Our structure of the VchCAST HIC reveals an arrangement wherein TnsC acts as a bifunctional adaptor, interacting with TniQ via its N-terminal face and with the STC via its C-terminal face (Fig. 2b). This architectural role of TnsC is similar to previous observations in ShCAST (type V-K)12 and PmcCAST (type I-B2) systems14,16. This modularity explains how CAST systems have diversified to co-opt a wide range of CRISPR effectors while preserving the core transposition mechanism.

A central question is how the targeting module is physically coupled to the core transposition machinery. In the HIC, TniQ2 serves as the primary physical bridge between the target recognition and transposition machinery (Fig. 3a), forming a predominantly hydrophobic interface with TnsC1 (Fig. 3b). Consistent with the functional importance of this interface, alanine substitutions at F2, L3 and F40 substantially reduced integration activity (Fig. 3c). TniQ forms a constitutive homodimer, but only the TniQ2 monomer interacts with TnsC, mirroring observations in the evolutionarily distant ShCAST and PmcCAST, in which a single TniQ subunit recruits TnsC12,16. Remarkably, despite the divergent overall architectures of the ShCAST (Protein Data Bank (PDB): 8EA3), PmcCAST (PDB: 8FF4) and VchCAST integration complexes, the TniQ–TnsC interface is notably conserved (Extended Data Fig. 5). In particular, the TnsC finger loop, previously shown to mediate critical TniQ interactions in ShCAST12, engages TniQ2 similarly in VchCAST (Extended Data Fig. 5). Consistent with this observation, truncations within the TnsC finger loop severely reduce transposition activity15. These findings identify the TniQ–TnsC interface as a shared docking point that may enable architecturally diverse CRISPR effectors to couple to common transposition machinery.

In a recent development, tnsB activity is strictly dependent on TnsC-mediated recruitment to the target site15, making these interactions central to understanding integration. We next examined how TnsB engages TnsC within the HIC, revealing multiple points of contact along the C-terminal face of TnsC, specifically at protomers TnsC2, TnsC3 and TnsC6 (Fig. 3d). Notably, the TBD of TnsB localizes to the TnsC2–TnsC3 interface (Fig. 3e), consistent with previous ShCAST and PmcCAST structures12,14 (Extended Data Fig. 6). Across Tn7-like transposons, ATP binding, but not hydrolysis, is required for integration activity26,27. AAA+ initiator clade regulators require ATP for oligomerization, as the ATP-binding pocket is formed at the inter-protomer interface28. This implies that transposition requires TnsC oligomerization on target DNA, although the mechanistic basis for this requirement has remained unclear. The conserved interaction between the TBD of TnsB and the TnsC inter-protomer interface now suggests that TnsB directly senses the oligomeric state of TnsC, providing a structural explanation for this long-standing observation.

In a recent development, another conserved feature across CAST systems is the interaction between TnsC and the extreme C terminus of TnsB, known as the hook, which is critical for transposition13. The interchangeability of TnsB hooks between type I-F3 CASTs29 underscores the importance of these structured interactions within otherwise disordered regions. Consistent with this role, we observe continuous density connecting the CTH (residues 563–573) of TnsB to the surface of TnsC6 (Fig. 3f), although additional contacts are likely to remain undetected owing to the length and extensive disorder of this region. The TnsB hook is predicted by AlphaFold 321 to correspond to the last eight residues of TnsB, an assignment supported by cryo-EM density observed in the HIC (Extended Data Fig. 7). The hook binding site in VchTnsC aligns well with ShTnsC13 and PmcTnsC14 (Extended Data Fig. 7), indicating that although structural details may differ, the binding location is conserved.

Recent findings suggest that having identified the TnsB hook interaction with TnsC, we reasoned that the disordered N- and C-terminal regions in all components of the core transposition machinery (TnsABC; Supplementary Fig. 12) could mediate additional interactions. Consistent with this idea, we observed contacts between the N terminus of TnsB and TnsA, and between the C-terminal tail of TnsC and TnsB (Fig. 3g). Residues 3–10 of the disordered N terminus of TnsB occupy a hydrophobic pocket on TnsA (Fig. 3h) close to aromatic residues F6 and F9, consistent with AlphaFold 3 predictions21 (Extended Data Fig. 1) and sequence conservation analysis (Extended Data Fig. 8a). Although N-terminal truncation (Δ1–10) caused a significant reduction in transposition activity, the TnsB F9A mutation reproduced almost none of this effect, suggesting that residues other than F9 mediate the relevant contacts within the truncated region (Extended Data Fig. 8c). The C-terminal tail of TnsC (residues 321–330) is positioned against the CTH of TnsB (Fig. 3i and Extended Data Fig. 8b) at a hydrophobic interface, also supported by AlphaFold 3 predictions21 (Supplementary Fig. 13) and conservation analysis (Extended Data Fig. 8b). The TnsC F329A mutation almost fully abrogated transposition activity, similar to the effect of C-terminal truncation of TnsC (Extended Data Fig. 8c). Analogous interactions between the C terminus of TnsC and the STC occur in PmcCAST, albeit involving different subunits and interfaces14 (Extended Data Fig. 9). These findings uncover a previously unrecognized network of interactions involving the unstructured termini of TnsA, TnsB and TnsC, revealing how the core transposition machinery may maintain associations to facilitate integration-competent assembly.

In a recent development, A previous cryo-EM structure of VchTnsC solved in the presence of DNA revealed an open heptameric ring-like arrangement in which the bound DNA was poorly resolved (PDB: 7UFI)15. In our HIC structure, although we clearly resolved the path of target DNA, no specific TnsC–DNA interactions could be precisely mapped. Thus, it is likely that the TnsC ring primarily associates with target DNA via the complementary basic surface formed by its central pore (Supplementary Fig. 14). This is consistent with previous data showing that TnsC binds DNA relatively weakly15, suggesting that TnsC requires partner proteins such as TniQ to initiate oligomerization on target DNA. Notably, comparison with PDB 7UFI reveals that the heptameric ring is significantly more open in the HIC. Aligning on TnsC1 results in an 11 Å displacement at TnsC7 relative to the equivalent protomer in PDB 7UFI (Fig. 3j), the result of an average 0.8 Å greater rise per protomer (Supplementary Fig. 15). This indicates that partner proteins induce larger conformational changes than those observed in TnsC with DNA alone. Our observations suggest that the oligomeric state of TnsC is sensitive to the presence of the partner proteins TniQ and TnsB and is mediated through distinct interaction interfaces located on specific TnsC protomers.

Recent findings suggest that we next investigated how TnsC is selectively recruited to the target site. The compositional heterogeneity of our reconstitution enabled us to resolve a free Cascade–TniQ complex (Extended Data Fig. 4) (TRC; 3.0 Å overall resolution; Fig. 4a) that closely resembles a prior structure of the target DNA-bound VchCAST Cascade–TniQ complex18 (Supplementary Fig. 16). This previously reported structure featured a partial R-loop and a disordered Cas8/5 helical bundle domain (HBD)18. By contrast, the Cascade–TniQ complex in the HIC (Fig. 4b) adopts a fully engaged conformation characterized by a complete R-loop and a structured Cas8/5 HBD. Comparison of Cascade–TniQ in the TRC and HIC structures reveals that R-loop completion is accompanied by a conformational change in TniQ2 to engage both target DNA and TnsC (Extended Data Fig. 10).
