Norway's ice hockey team notes Russia replacing it at World Juniors

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that with just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant.
  • The move, which has yet to be publicly revealed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play.
  • The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that with just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association remarked the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

The move, which has yet to be publicly revealed by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF said it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey.".

According to recent reports, as of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," remarked Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

How this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been noted about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days.".

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

"We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who said he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius mentioned Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

Sources indicate that "However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could matter visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions currently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," stated spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius noted he didn't wish to "speculate on implications.".

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the issue could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

Two teams enjoying solid campaigns in Spain's top flight thus far will lock horns on Sunday evening, as Real Sociedad welcome Sevilla to Anoeta Stadium.

Real Sociedad just about lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides, having posted 55 victories to Sevilla's 52, while 35 of their 142 fixtures have finished level.

Real Sociedad will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-1 defeat to Crystal Palace in the Europa League, with the result leaving them down in 27th spot in the overall table and out of the knockout round playoffs at this stage of proceedings.

It has been a struggle for Real Sociedad in Europe this season, and they were also beaten 3-2 by Racing de Santander in Spain's top flight last weekend, so the Basque team will be bidding to avoid a third straight loss in all competitions on Sunday night.

La Real have had a strong campaign in Spain's top flight, with a record of seven wins, one draw and five defeats from 13 matches bringing them 22 points, which is enough for fifth spot in the La Liga table.

Pellegrino Matarazzo's side now have three straight league games against Sevilla, Real Madrid and Villarreal before returning to European action at home to Torreense on December 10.

Real Sociedad have been strong at home in the league this season, boasting a record of four wins, one draw and one defeat, picking up 13 points from six matches.

Sevilla have won five, drawn four and lost four of their 13 league matches this season, with 19 points leaving them in sixth spot in the table, three points behind fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

The Red and Whites are without a win in their last three La Liga fixtures, though, losing at Getafe at the start of the month before drawing back-to-back games with Alaves and Real Betis.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only actually won one of their last seven league matches, but sitting sixth after 13 games represents a solid start to the campaign.

Sevilla recorded a 1-0 win over Real Sociedad when the two teams last locked horns in May 2026, but the corresponding game last season ended in a 2-1 success for the Basque outfit.

Los Nervionenses have picked up eight points from their six away league matches during the 2026-27 campaign courtesy of a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Andoni Iraola has done a pretty decent job since being appointed as Liverpool's manager.

He's managed to get his team to fourth in the Premier League table with only seven points separating them from first-placed Arsenal.

Obviously, this is still a decent number of points to chip away at but, if the Gunners continue dropping points by drawing games against teams such as Newcastle, the Reds could find themselves back in the title race soon.

Nobody knows what lies ahead for any team but, if Liverpool manage to pull off even half of the transfers they've been linked with, they'll be storming their way up the table.

And to make things even sweeter, the perfect signing for Iraola has just emerged.

Arhcie Brown has a £19.2 million release clause in his contract.

So many areas among Liverpool's ranks still need upgrading.

This is a horrible thing to write as, across the last couple of years, well over £600 million has been spent on fresh players by the Reds.

Some of the transfers that they've made have worked out for the better but, others haven't quite hit the mark.

Milos Kerkez is an example of this because, even though he has had a fair few decent performances, his inconsistency is terrible.

Some days he can be seen as the Premier League's best left-back and, on others, he could end up being the worst player on the pitch.

This has forced fans to ask for a new left-back with Florian Plettenberg now sharing a rather intriguing patch on Liverpool target, Archie Brown.

"Archie Brown has a release clause worth around €23m, valid for both the winter and summer transfer windows. The 23 y/o is a regular starter at Fenerbahçe and has also impressed with some very strong performances in the Champions League," he wrote.

"Under contract until 2028, a move is planned, with Premier League clubs already making enquiries.".

Archie Brown would fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans.

Not only would Brown be classed as homegrown but, he'd also be one of the cheapest transfers on the market.

Recent links with Liverpool and Alejandro Balde have emerged with Barcelona demanding close to €50 million for the Spaniard.

Others such as Daniel Svensson have also been linked with a move but, again, Borussia Dortmund want over €40 million for him.

Each of these players would be exceptional additions but, Brown for €23 million (£19 million) is a deal that's too good to pass up.

He put in the performance of a lifetime when Liverpool faced Fenerbahce earlier in the season and, if he can replicate that form in the Premier League, the Reds would be onto a winner.

Liverpool signing Brown would also give Kerkez a genuine challenger for his position which might even help him develop his performance.

Since the price for Brown is so good, Liverpool will have to act fast and get straight on with securing his services when the January transfer window opens up, otherwise, they'll end up kicking themselves for missing out on it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it looked like they had been knocked to the floor for good in the Europa League, AC Milan got up and produced a stunning response in Greece.

Sources indicate that la Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin their analysis this morning by writing that Milan showed their ‘true Italian colours in Europe at last’ in a ‘magnificent, incredible performance’. It took a while to get going, with two goals from the home side needed as a wake-up call, but it worked.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim reshaped his side and they produced epic comeback, turning a 0–2 deficit into a 4–2 victory, with the Rossoneri suddenly appearing courageous, aggressive, and dominant. For one night, Omari Hutchinson was the god of Athens, with his Messi-like goal and two assists.

In stoppage time, the tireless Diego Moreira also got on the scoresheet. It’s a massive boost to both energy and morale, putting the team back into the play-off places. There is more work to be done, but it feels like a start.

Also worth examining is the Milan side seen in the first half and the beginning of the second, a period when Joao Silva’s quick goal to make it 2-0 threatened to turn into yet another cursed night.

The Rossoneri were off the pace again, completely at the mercy of Olympiacos’s frenetic pace and 4-2-3-1 formation, which hemmed them into the final thirty metres and stifled any chance of a counter-attack.

It was a case of no Luke Modric, no party. In truth, one counter did materialise, coming down the left flank. Despite being off-balance, the ever-present Cissé managed to get a shot on target from the ground, only for Pirola – an Italian playing in Greece – to clear it off the line.

Milan need to be built around Cissé, but in the first half it was Goncalo Ramos who occupied the centre of the 3-4-2-1, functioning less as a ‘false nine’ and more as a centre-forward who simply wasn’t there, much like the team-mates who should have been supporting him.

Milan got off to a poor start. Entrusting the protection of the midfield to the Jashari-Rabiot duo – neither of whom are a true defensive specialist – proved to be a questionable strategy against Freuler and Gustavo Sà.

In a recent development, in truth, the whole side struggled. Hutchinson was ineffective as a right-sided attacking midfielder; Cissé was never brought into play on the opposite flank; and Estupiñán – tasked with a hybrid role as both full-back and wing-back – looked completely flat on the left.

It has been revealed that amorim’s tactical experiments backfired, not least because De Winter was far from flawless at the back, while Diawara appeared somewhat naive. At the other end, Pirola looked every bit the Achilles among the Greeks.

He scored the opening goal with a header (officially recorded by UEFA as an own goal, as the ball ricocheted off the crossbar and then Maignan), and later made a crucial intervention to deny Cissé.

One could have held endless debates over why Milan wins five out of six matches in Italy, yet was on the verge of a fourth defeat in Europe. Arguments about the ‘pace of European competition’ feel a bit reductive: fair enough regarding Benfica, but we are talking about Ferencváros and Olympiacos.

Milan simply needed to restore their balance. Amorim took drastic measures: he brought on Yunus Musah to bolster the midfield and Pulisic to inject energy into the attack, while taking off Estupiñán and Ramos (the latter due to a knock), effectively reshaping the entire side.

Recent findings suggest that in defence, Mario Gila and Koni De Winter remained (though Fikayo Tomori, who soon replaced the latter, performed much better), joined by Sankhoun Diawara. In the middle, Hutchinson and Moreira took the flanks, while the well-balanced duo of Jashari and Musah took control of the centre.

Industry observers note that up front, Rabiot and Pulisic flanked Cissé. When Jota Silva made it 2–0 just four minutes in, it seemed as though there was no effective remedy, but it was merely a matter of regrouping.

According to recent reports, moving away from his hybrid role as an attacking midfielder/central midfielder, Hutchinson transformed into a devastating wide player. In the 11th minute of the second half he won the ball in midfield, embarks on a brilliant slalom run and found the bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that from that moment on, the Greek side effectively disappeared from the match. They ran around aimlessly, lacking any tactical cohesion or ideas, while their manager Alguacil faltered with his substitutions.

The equaliser came from Cissé, who headed home a pinpoint assist from Hutchinson after more good work on the right. It was his tenth goal of the season (four in the Europa League, six in Serie A): when Cissé plays he scores, simple as that.

Recent findings suggest that the 3-2 goal arrived courtesy of Pulisic, who executed a stunning mid-air half-volley, once again set up by the Englishman. Pulisic himself squanders a chance to make it 4-2 on the counter-attack, but Moreira eventually sealed the deal in the closing seconds.

In a recent development, it can’t be remarked that ‘we’ve found the real Milan’ even after the comeback, not with a Milan that possesses so many different identities. It’s clear that Ramos needs to reflect, but the urgent need for points suggests it’s time for Cissé and Pulisic.

In a recent development, A defensive-minded player is a must in a two-man midfield. If Hutchison is such a dynamo on the right, then Moreira could perhaps be ‘sacrificed’ on the left. And at the back, maybe Tomori was cast aside a bit too soon.

Half the squad is sidelined with injuries, yet there are more resources available than one might imagine. Six points is not enough: the team need another six from their last three games to make the knockouts. The night in Piraeus, however, is a start.

Meanwhile, the Bluebirds make the journey across South Wales sitting nine points adrift of their hosts.

With Freyr Alexandersson still deliberating over whether he intends to leave Rosenborg and if that move may be delayed until December, Ashley Williams will remain as interim boss for this game.

The Swansea legend has only accumulated one point from games against West Bromwich Albion and Middlesbrough, yet his side came from behind to earn a share of the spoils versus the Baggies and pushed leaders Boro all the way at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night.

Those 2-2 and 1-2 scorelines versus the fifth and first-placed teams in the division suggest that Williams has had a positive effect on the group after Vitor Matos's surprise switch to Strasbourg.

Nevertheless, this remains a Swansea outfit that have lost five of their last seven Championship fixtures, their only success being a 4-0 victory at home to Blackburn Rovers.

Despite that drop off in form, Swansea remain just eight points off top spot, emphasising that a win in this contest will keep them in contention with the teams above them ahead of Alexandersson's potential arrival.

As for Cardiff, they are reeling from the shock 4-0 defeat at home to struggling Preston North End in midweek.

Not only did the Bluebirds lose their eight-match unbeaten record at the Cardiff City Stadium, they have now conceded 11 goals across their last three home contests.

Brian Barry-Murphy's side now sit just six points above the relegation zone at a time when they are still searching for their first away success since earning promotion back to the second tier.

However, it should be noted that their last two away games have been at Wolverhampton Wanderers and Norwich City, two of three teams in the division that have collected 16 points across their last six matches.

Cardiff travel to Swansea having failed to win any of their last four games at the Swansea.com Stadium, losing three times without scoring before a 1-1 draw on their most recent visit in August 2024.

Swansea City Championship form:.

Cardiff City Championship form:.

Having served a one-match ban, Swansea left-back Josh Tymon will return to the starting lineup.

However, Marko Stamenic is still absent through suspension, while Goncalo Franco and Ronald are expected to remain on the sidelines.

Jay Fulton and Zan Vipotnik are pushing for recalls in midfield and attack respectively.

With several defenders sidelined, including Perry Ng who is still having a knee injury assessed, Barry-Murphy may not make any changes to his Cardiff backline.

Nevertheless, David Turnbull, Joel Colwill and Chris Willock are all in contention for returns in midfield and the final third.

Swansea City possible starting lineup:.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Welsh, Cabango, Tymon; Just, Fulton, Eustaquio; Opoku, Vipotnik, Eom.

Cardiff City possible starting lineup:.

Trott; Kpakio, Fish, Bielik, Bagan; Robertson; Tanner, Moylan, R Colwill, Willock; Salech.

While Cardiff are expected to deliver a response to their capitulation to Preston, we cannot ignore that Swansea have been competitive against top teams under Williams's short tenure. Therefore, the Swans get our backing in this fixture, albeit with a winning goal potentially coming during the closing stages.

OUT OF THIS WORLD! Celtic link up with data analytics firm Pluto to improve recruitment

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 15:52 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Celtic have confirmed a long-term partnership with a firm the club believe will transform their recruitment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 15:52 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:32 EST, 25 November 2026.

Celtic have confirmed a long-term partnership with a firm the club believe will transform their recruitment.

Recent findings suggest that london-based Pluto Data Analytics use predictive analytics and AI to help football clubs with player identification. The initial deal lasts three years, with scope for extension.

Celtic believe the deal will ‘support the club’s continuing commitment to innovation and excellence in football operations by enhancing recruitment analysis, talent identification, squad planning and broader football decision-making processes.’.

The Parkhead club’s recruitment strategy has been heavily criticised by supporters in recent seasons amid their struggles in Europe and increased domestic competition from Rangers and Hearts.

A statement explaining the arrangement added: ‘The partnership forms part of Celtic’s ongoing investment in modern football infrastructure and its commitment to ensuring that football decisions are informed by the best available intelligence and expertise.

‘By working with Pluto Data Analytics, Celtic will gain access to enhanced analytical tools and insights to support its existing recruitment and football operations functions.

The Parkhead club are hoping that newly introduced deal will improve their recruitment process.

‘The objective is clear: to improve decision-making, identify emerging opportunities and support the club’s long-term football strategy.’.

The move comes following long-standing criticism that the Scottish champions’ means of scouting undervalued talents had become outdated, with their failure to act swiftly and efficiently in the transfer market leading to repeated failures in the European qualification rounds.

Rival clubs such as Hearts have benefited from the use of data thanks to the access they have had to Jamestown Analytics.

‘We are always looking for ways to strengthen our football operation and ensure that we continue to evolve in an increasingly competitive environment,’ remarked Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson.

‘We have been reviewing the options in this area in order to select the optimum model for our club.

‘Our partnership with Pluto Data Analytics, an organisation with real quality and pedigree within this field, reflects our commitment to innovation and continuous improvement.

O'Neill notes he hopes partnership 'will help us deliver the success we are all striving for'.

In a recent development, ‘Recruitment remains one of the most vital areas of any football club. Our aim is to identify talent as effectively as possible, reduce uncertainty where we can and support our football staff with the best available information.

‘We believe this partnership will strengthen our ability to support the club’s ambitions both domestically and in European competition.’.

Manager Martin O’Neill added: ‘I am very pleased that Celtic and Pluto are joining together to give the club an extra level of insight and analysis which is becoming more prominent in football.

‘While football is not an exact science, if the club can access and utilise new tools and new details, ultimately, we hope that such data will help us deliver the success we are all striving for.

Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson says Pluto deal is 'optimum model' for the club.

According to recent reports, ‘Our recruitment and wider football operations teams have already engaged with Pluto. Our aims in the short, medium and longer term are being developed and we are confident that our relationship will deliver real tangible benefit to the club over the next few years.’.

Jon Godfrey, CEO of Pluto Data Analytics, said: ‘Today is a big day for Pluto and we are incredibly excited to be working with Celtic, one of the biggest clubs in world football.

‘We believe that predictive data modelling combined with the allure and resources of such a famous institution will allow us to achieve great things in this partnership.

‘Celtic has the capacity to compete at the highest levels of European football and it is an honour and a fantastic challenge to work relentlessly with the club on achieving the exciting goals we have put in place.’.
